e: Tiny glucose sugars link hand-in-hand like busy snap beads to build tough plant walls called cellulose.

q: What is the ultimate purpose of the Calvin cycle?
a: To convert carbon dioxide into sugars
To convert waste products to oxygen
To convert sugars, fatty acids, and amino acids into ATP
To separate water into hydrogen and oxygen
e: Inside green leaves, this clever cycle catches invisible carbon dioxide from the air and bakes it into sweet, energizing sugars.

q: Which of the following is the most common long-term storage form of energy for vertebrate animals:
e: Animals pack away cozy fats, called lipids, like hidden treasure chests to save up lots of long-term energy.

q: A liver cell has stopped functioning and a scientist observes that it is producing lactic acid. Failure of what organelle [organ-ELL] most likely caused the liver cell to stop functioning?
e: When a cell's mighty powerhouse, the mitochondrion, fizzles out, the poor liver scrambles and brews sour lactic acid instead.

q: Which of the following hormones requires iodine for its synthesis?
e: Your body snaps bits of iodine into place to build thyroxine, a special messenger that keeps your engine humming.

q: Which of the following ocean organisms is the predator of an oyster?
e: A sea star hugs an oyster tight with tiny tube feet, prying its shell open for a tasty seabed snack.

q: Of the following habitats, which is the most likely to have the highest amount of biodiversity?
e: Warm, rainy tropical rainforests are bursting with more colorful critters and buzzing life than anywhere else on Earth!

q: Which of the following statements regarding corals and zooxanthellae [zoh-uh-zan-THEL-ee] is FALSE?
a: Corals can live for a few months without their zooxanthellae
When a coral bleaches the zooxanthellae die
The color of a coral tissue is largely due to the zooxanthellae
Increased water temperature can prompt a bleaching event
e: Stressed corals do not kill their algae partners during bleaching; they just evict them into the water, hoping to reunite later.

q: In the symbiotic relationship that allows survival of lichens, which of the following is the photosynthetic component?
e: In this cozy lichen team, cheerful green algae acts like a sun-powered kitchen, cooking up food for its fungal friend.

q: Which of the following characteristics suggests that RNA was formed before DNA?
e: Ancient RNA could do real chemical work all by itself, acting like a handy tool to help life before DNA appeared.

q: Which of the following is NOT a mechanism plants use to disperse their seeds?
e: Apomixis is a clever way plants create seeds without pollen, not a travel plan to scatter them across the meadow!

q: Which of the following enzymes assists in digestion of starches and complex sugars?
e: Meet amylase, your spit's cheerful little scissors that snips big, chewy starches into sweet, bite-sized sugar treats.

q: Which of the following structures would likely be the most resistant to heat denaturation?
e: A bacterial endospore is like a sleeping germ inside heat-proof armor, built tough to survive boiling temperatures without melting.

q: Which of the following processes does not add carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
e: While other processes puff carbon dioxide out, hungry green leaves breathe it in during photosynthesis to make food.

q: Why are so-called nectar robbers a problem for plants?
a: They do not help pollinate plants
e: Sneaky bugs chew through petals to sip sweet nectar, running off without carrying any pollen to help the flower.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about slime mold?
a: It lacks chitin in its cell walls
e: Even with mold in its name, slime mold is actually a clever protist that wanders around eating, not a real fungus!

q: In which of the following locations found in the human body is the hormone somatotropin produced?
e: Tucked beneath your brain, the tiny pituitary gland works hard making somatotropin to help you grow big and tall.

q: Which of the following plant groups includes mosses, liverworts, and hornworts?
e: Soft green mosses belong to the bryophyta family, hugging damp rocks like tiny velvet carpets without needing any true roots!

q: The semicircular canals in the ears are responsible for which of the following functions?
e: Deep inside your ears, little fluid-filled loops swirl around like tiny levels to keep your balance so you do not tumble over!

q: Which of the following animals is most closely related in phylogeny [fye-LAW-jen-ee] to a slug?
e: Believe it or not, the octopus is a soft-bodied mollusk cousin to the slug, just swimming with eight arms instead!

q: A diatom is an example of what?
e: Meet the diatom, a tiny creature in shiny glass armor that belongs to the wonderful world of protists.

q: Which of the following best explains the phenomenon of industrial melanism in moths?
a: Darker moths were better camouflaged from predators and were selected for
Moths became darker over time as more soot accumulated within their bodies
Increased soot caused individual moths to alter their pigment levels, which propagated to later generations
Moths actively changed their camouflage patterns to camouflage better
e: With soot coating the trees, darker moths hid better from hungry predators, so nature selected them to survive and flourish.

q: Anatomy considers the forms of macroscopic structures such as organs and organ systems.
e: It is true that anatomy explores the big, amazing structures you can actually see, like organs and bones!

q: Which of the following portions of the small intestine receives food directly from the stomach?
e: The duodenum is the very first stretch of the small intestine, welcoming dinner the second it tumbles out of the stomach.

q: Human infants weighing more or less than the average birth weight of 6 to 8 pounds have a greater chance of mortality. Which of the following types of natural selection describes this phenomenon?
e: Stabilizing selection favors the cozy middle, helping average-weight babies thrive by steering clear of risky extremes.

q: In human biology, a circadium rhythm relates to a period of roughly how many hours?
e: Tucked inside you is a cozy little clock that runs for roughly 24 hours, deciding when you wake up and when you yawn.

q: Which of the following locations in a chloroplast has the highest acidity?
e: During photosynthesis, tiny hydrogen particles pack inside the thylakoid lumen, making this pocket the chloroplast's most acidic spot.

q: Which of the following is true when alligators are behaving territorially?
a: They run full force at the threat
Slap their tails on the ground
Open their jaws while making a clicking noise
They bellow while showing their tail and neck
e: To say this swamp is mine, a grumpy alligator arches its neck, lifts its tail, and roars a deep bellow.

q: Over hundreds of years, a population of black worms slowly stratifies into a group of ground-dwelling worms and a group of tree-dwelling worms. What type of isolation is observed here?
e: Because some worms chose leafy tree penthouses while others preferred cozy dirt basements, their separate homes kept them apart through habitat isolation.

q: Which of the following is found in both prokaryotic [PRO-care-ee-AW-tic] and eukaryotic [YOU-care-ee-AW-tic] cells?
e: Every living cell needs protein factories to survive, so little ribosomes show up in both simple and complex cells.

q: Which of the following terms do biologists most often use to describe animals that do not move by their own design or effort:
e: Like barnacles glued to a seaside rock, creatures that never move on their own are called sessile.

q: What property of water gives it such a high specific heat?
e: Water molecules hug each other with tight hydrogen bonds, stubbornly refusing to heat up without tons of energy!

q: What type of solution can cause plasmolysis of a plant cell when the cell is immersed in the solution?
e: A hypertonic bath is so thirsty it sucks water outward, causing the plant cell to shrink and pull away.

q: All of the following cells undergo mitosis EXCEPT:
e: Red blood cells give up their nucleus to carry oxygen, meaning they cannot divide through mitosis like other cells.

q: Which of the following organs is responsible for maintaining blood sugar 4 hours after a meal?
e: Hours after lunch, your trusty liver gently releases stored sugar into your blood to keep your energy humming along!

q: Which of the following organelles would be most abundant in cells that are producing large amounts of ATP through oxidative metabolism:
e: Mitochondria are the mighty powerhouses of the cell, happily churning out energetic ATP sparkplugs to keep things running.

q: Which of the following is the closest synonym for motile:
e: If a little creature is motile, it possesses the wonderful gift of being able to move around.

q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of down feathers?
a: Trapping a layer of air to act as insulation
Waterproofing the outer layer of the bird
Providing contouring to make the bird more aerodynamic
e: Down feathers act like a bird's fluffy winter jacket, trapping warm pockets of air to keep them cozy!

q: Which of the following is a vitamin D deficiency disease of the young, often marked by the faulty ossification of bone?
e: Without sunshine vitamin D, growing bones turn soft and bendy instead of super strong, causing a condition called rickets.

q: Which of the following is NOT a cartilaginous fish?
e: Unlike sharks made of bendy cartilage, an eel carries a skeleton of real, hard bones inside its slippery body.

q: In humans, which of the following is the name for the tube that makes up the complete digestive system?
e: From your first crunchy bite to the very end, food travels down one continuous winding highway called the alimentary canal.

q: Which is not a basic muscle type in the human body?
e: Smooth, skeletal, and cardiac are your body's three true muscle types, while ventricular is just a room inside your heart.

q: In the spring of 2013, scientists from the University of Michigan and Louisiana State University predicted that a particular coastal region of the US would experience a record breaking dead-zone. For what region was this prediction made?
e: Farm runoff washed into the Gulf of Mexico, stealing the water's oxygen and creating a massive dead zone.

q: Which of the following genetic mutations would cause the greatest change in the nucleotide sequence of a gene?
e: Slipping in just one extra base shifts the entire reading frame, scrambling every single three-letter genetic word that comes after!

q: Which of the following is a distinguishing characteristic of cheetah paws?
a: Their claws are covered with a sheath of skin
e: Cheetahs cannot fully pull their claws back, using them like built-in cleats to grip the ground during speedy chases!

q: Which of the following is not a case of symbiosis:
e: Critters share life through mutualism, parasitism, or commensalism, but formatism is completely made up and not a real partnership!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about emphysema?
a: Emphysema makes people progressively shorter of breath
Smoking is the leading cause of emphysema
Pulmonary rehabilitation can reverse the damage from emphysema
Pneumothorax [noo-muh-THOHR-aks] is a possible complication of emphysema
e: Special breathing exercises help folks stay active, but they cannot magically rebuild the lung tissue emphysema has already damaged.

q: Approximately how long is a year on Uranus?
e: That chilly blue giant takes a whopping 84 Earth years just to complete one slow orbit around the sun.

q: Which of the following terms describes the ability of a mutation in gene X to affect the expression of gene Y?
e: With epistasis, one gene acts like a sneaky boss, stepping in to control how another gene shows up.

q: What is the correct term for a marine organism whose internal salt concentration varies with that of their environment?
e: Instead of fighting the salty sea, easygoing osmoconformers simply match their inside saltiness to the water around them!

q: Digestion begins in the mouth because saliva contains salivary amylase [AM-ill-ace]. What macromolecule does amylase digest?
e: Amylase in your spit acts like hungry little scissors, quickly chopping giant starchy pretzels into tiny, sweet bits.

q: About how old is Earth?
e: Our grand home planet has been spinning around the warm sun for about four and a half billion wondrous years.

q: Which of the following is an abiotic factor that would most greatly affect the presence of an Archaea species typically found in ocean thermal vents?
e: These tiny, tough microbes depend on the scorching water temperature bubbling from deep vents to survive in the dark ocean.

q: An individual with Turner syndrome has which of the following genotypes?
e: Most girls start life with two X chromosomes, but someone with Turner syndrome is born with just one, labeled XO.

q: Which of the following DNA mutations is most likely to occur?
e: Adenine and guanine share similar twin shapes, making an A-to-G swap the easiest puzzle mix-up for cells to make.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
e: Mitochondria are the mighty little power plants of the cell, busily churning out ATP energy to keep you zooming around!

q: Your neighbor just cut down a tree that he claims germinated the year he was born. What do you need to count to determine the plausibility of your neighbor's story?
e: Each year, a growing tree builds new water-drinking tubes called xylem rings, marking its birthdays like secret wooden candles!

q: DNA ligase [LYE-gase] is an enzyme that catalyzes which of the following reactions?
e: DNA ligase acts like tiny magical glue, building phosphodiester bonds to stitch broken strands neatly back together.

q: Which of the following is a reptile:
e: With its tough, scaly shell and love of sunbathing, the snapping turtle is a true reptile, unlike its slimy amphibian neighbors!

q: Which of the following is the BEST explanation of why DDT was such a problem for raptors:
a: it is stable and accumulates in animals as it moves up the food chain
it causes extreme light sensitivity and since raptors have no eye lids it causes them to go blind quickly
it is highly concentrated in the kidneys of mice which are a main food source of most raptors
raptors are extremely sensitive to very low doses of DDT and it causes immediate death on exposure
e: This sneaky chemical did not disappear; it piled up inside tiny critters and grew more dangerous as big birds ate them.

q: Which of the following types of enzymes would most likely be involved in changing glucose-6-phosphate to glucose-1-phosphate?
e: An isomerase acts like a clever puzzle solver, rearranging the sugar's parts into a new shape without losing a single piece.

q: Which of the following genetic traits would be most expected to increase in prevalence in the population over time?
a: A genetic variant in a deer population that results in a skeletal difference that causes the deer to move more slowly
A genetic variation that leads to behavioral changes due to a decreased fear of predators
A genetic mutation in a mammal that increases the nutrients available in the milk, so that the offspring grow stronger and faster
A genetic mutation that increases the size of the teeth in the mouth, reducing the space available for food in the mouth and eliminating some food choices.
e: Super-nutritious milk helps baby animals grow strong and healthy, making it much easier for them to survive and share that helpful trait!

q: Which of the following will NOT alter a somatic cell's genome during an organism's lifetime?
e: Meiosis only makes reproductive cells like eggs and sperm, so it never changes the genes inside your everyday body cells!

q: Which of the following animals would NOT be classified in the phylum [FY-luhm] cnidaria [ny-DAIR-ee-uh]?
e: While jellyfish and anemones are stinging cnidarians, the prickly sea urchin belongs to the spiny-skinned echinoderm family instead.

q: Which of the following types of molecules is not generally composed of a long chain of monomers?
e: Unlike giant chains of repeating building blocks, a fatty acid is just a single tidy molecule standing on its own.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the human eye:
a: the cornea acts as a lens with a fixed shape
images that are formed on the retina are inverted
most of the eye is filled with a liquid called the aqueous humor
vitamin A is important for light absorbing molecules critical in vision
e: Most of our eyeball is actually packed with squishy vitreous jelly, not the watery aqueous liquid up front.

q: Which of the following is the scientific class to which spider belong?
e: With eight busy legs and no antennae, a spider proudly spins its web as a card-carrying arachnid, not an insect!

q: When a nerve message reaches the end of an axon it sends a message or impulse across the space between the nerves to continue its message to the next nerve by a substance best known as:
e: Tiny chemical messengers called neurotransmitters happily leap across the gap between nerves to pass along the brain's secret notes.

q: Imagine you are dropped at a random place on planet Earth. You are not told where you are. However, you are told that the average temperature here is 78 Fahrenheit and that over 180 inches of rain fall here every year. In what kind of biome do you most likely find yourself?
e: Tropical rain forests stay delightfully warm and get drenched in non-stop showers, making them the wettest, coziest spots on Earth.

q: Stromatolites [stroh-MAT-oh-lite] have been used to study the age of which of the following?
e: Stromatolites are rocky castles built by microscopic critters billions of years ago, showing us what Earth's very first life looked like.

q: What is the term for the structure that implants into the endometrium during mammalian development?
e: Before growing into a baby, a tiny ball of cells called a blastocyst snuggles safely into the cozy womb wall.

q: Which of the following characteristics is MOST typical of bacteria:
e: Bacteria are tiny, carefree wanderers that carry their genetic recipes loose inside, never bothering to build a central nucleus room.

q: Which of the following statements about microbial growth is most accurate?
a: Microorganisms in the environment always grow at their maximum rate
A given microbial species will usually grow faster in the environment than is possible in the laboratory
Prolonged exponential growth in the environment is rare for microorganisms
In the laboratory, growth slows when microorganisms are grown in pure culture
e: In the wild, hungry germs quickly run out of snacks and room, so endless, explosive population booms are super rare.

q: Which of the following is a set of reactions that do NOT require light and where carbon dioxide is used to make 3 carbon sugar phosphate molecules that are later used to make 6 carbon sugars:
e: Deep inside leaves, the clever Calvin cycle works without sunlight, using captured carbon dioxide to bake sweet sugar molecules.

q: Which of the following trees is NOT a gymnosperm [JIM- nuh-spurm]?
e: Unlike cone-bearing gymnosperms, the proud magnolia shows off gorgeous blooming flowers to wrap up its seeds as an angiosperm.

q: Actin and myosin are proteins most directly associated with the function of which of the following tissues or systems of the human body?
e: Actin and myosin work like microscopic tug-of-war partners, pulling tight to help your mighty muscles flex and move!

q: Which of the following birds depends almost entirely on man-made nesting boxes in the eastern United States?
e: Purple martins love human neighbors so much that in the east, they raise their chicks almost entirely inside cozy birdhouses we build for them!

q: Pepsin is most active in the stomach due to the presence of which of the following acids?
e: Meet pepsin, a hungry little belly helper who needs sour hydrochloric acid to wake up and chomp your lunch!

q: In bean and corn seeds, the food supply that is used by the seed to germinate and grow is found in the:
e: Think of the cotyledon as a cozy lunchbox, feeding the tiny baby sprout until it can taste sunshine!

q: What happens to the population of white blood cells when a bacterial infection occurs?
e: Your body sounds the alarm and rushes out whole armies of brave white blood cells to battle the invading germs!

q: Plants are important to our ecosystem because they convert solar energy into which of the following forms of energy?
e: Green leaves catch warm sunbeams and magically bake that light into sweet chemical energy to feed the world.

q: During which of the following embryonic stages of a human are all 3 germ layers formed:
e: During the gastrula stage, a tiny growing baby folds its cells into all three body layers, like a cozy blanket.

q: What is the endocrine gland that controls how the body regulates metabolism and is associated with Graves' disease?
e: Perched in your neck like a butterfly, the thyroid gland sets your body's energy speed and gets overexcited in Graves' disease.

q: Where would you find squalene?
a: In the head of a sperm whale
In the intestines of a sperm whale
In the liver of a shark
In the stomach of a shark
e: Sharks pack lightweight squalene oil inside their big livers, helping them float like magic through the deep blue ocean.

q: What is the connective tissue that protects the ends of the bones and allows them to move more easily?
e: Cartilage acts like a slippery, rubbery pillow on bone ends, helping them glide smoothly past each other whenever you wiggle.

q: Which of the following is a monocot:
e: Zea maize, our friendly corn, is a monocot because each little seed sprouts into the world with just one baby leaf!

q: You go to the doctor because you have a sore throat. She looks at your throat and sympathizes, then says, "Go home and rest, you'll beat that virus in no time!" She does NOT write a prescription for antibiotics, however, because:
a: Antibiotics kill bacteria and you have a viral infection
Antibiotics only work if you have a cold
e: Antibiotics only target pesky bacteria, so they are completely powerless against the sneaky little viruses causing your sniffles.

q: What is the name for the basic five carbon sugar that is present in slightly different forms in both DNA and RNA nucleotides:
e: Ribose is the sweet five-sided sugar that holds hands with other pieces to build your DNA and RNA instructions.

q: Under which of the following conditions would a plant's stomata most likely be open?
e: Thirsty leaves open their tiny breathing pores in cold, moist air because they can sip fresh air without drying out.

q: Yenla is studying how a moth population changes over time. Her first sample indicates that 7500 are spotted and 2500 are striped. Ten years later, she samples the same area and finds that 3000 of the moths are spotted and 7000 are striped. What evolutionary process is occurring?
e: Directional selection happens because nature nudged the moth family toward one new look, shifting the whole group toward groovy stripes.

q: Which of the following sets of two light colors do chloroplast pigments absorb most effectively during photosynthesis?
e: Plants reflect green light away, but they hungrily drink up red and blue light to power their food factories.

q: The process of nitrogen fixation is extremely energy intensive due to which of the following?
a: Atoms of free nitrogen are triply bound to other nitrogen atoms
Atoms of free nitrogen are highly reactive
The nitrogen atom is highly unreactive
Nitrogen atoms are usually found tightly bound to alkaline earth metals
e: Nitrogen atoms hug each other with a super-tight triple bond, so it takes a mountain of energy to pull them apart.

q: If you were a pirate in the 15th century, you might very well suffer from scurvy. In order to prevent the disease, which of the following should you consume?
e: Juicy oranges are packed with sunny vitamin C, which keeps old-time sailing pirates healthy and saves them from scurvy.

q: What type of animal tissue is found in the ears and nose as structural support?
e: Bendy, rubbery cartilage gives your nose and ears their springy shape so you can wiggle them without snapping bone.

q: How many baby/milk teeth does a human child have in total?
e: Little kids show off twenty baby teeth before the Tooth Fairy trades them in for grown-up ones!

q: In humans, ovulation usually occurs how many days before the start of the next menstrual period:
e: Like clockwork, the body gently releases an egg fourteen days before the next monthly period begins.

q: Which of the following statements about human intestinal fluid is NOT true?
a: It is a clear, yellow fluid
Five or six liters of intestinal fluid are produced each day
It has a slightly basic pH of 7.6
e: Your tummy makes only one or two liters of digestive juice each day, not five or six, which would simply be too much!

q: If a pea plant with white flowers is crossed with a pea plant with red flowers and all 100 seedlings from this cross are white, then which of the following statements is most likely true:
a: white flowers are dominant in all flowering plants
red flowers are recessive in all flowering plants
e: Because all one hundred baby flowers bloomed white, the white trait completely hid the red one, proving that white is dominant.

q: Which of the following statements is true about meiosis [my-OH-sis]?
a: In the first meiotic division, sister chromatids separate
The second meiotic division results in four haploid daughter cells
Crossing over occurs during the second meiotic [my-AW-tik] division
Individual chromatids line up at the midzone for separation during metaphase I
e: After one cell does two grand splits, it proudly welcomes four tiny daughter cells, each with half the usual instructions.

q: Which of the following kinds of mammal teeth are used to bite and cut?
e: Sitting right up front like sharp little blades, your incisors cleanly snip and cut into crunchy apples every lunchtime.

q: A defibrillator is used to start up a heartbeat once a heart has stopped beating.
e: A defibrillator cannot restart a heart that fully stopped; it actually resets a wildly fluttering heartbeat back to its calm, steady rhythm.

q: Conservation biology tries to preserve which of the following ecosystem characteristics?
a: Large population size for all inhabiting species
Large population size for all inhabiting mammals
Elevated biodiversity for all forms of life
Elevated biodiversity for all macroscopic forms of life
e: Nature loves a full house, so conservation works like a giant hug protecting every kind of living thing, big or microscopic!

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding heterochromatin [hetero- CROW-ma-tin]?
a: It consists of DNA loosely wound around histones
During mitosis [my-TOW-sis], most nuclear DNA is found as heterochromatin
Chromatin [CROW-mah-tin] organization is determined by DNA modifications
e: When a cell divides in mitosis, its DNA neatly packs into super-tight bundles called heterochromatin for safe travel.

q: In 1665, what person, using a microscope he built, observed perforations in plant stems, which he called cells:
e: Robert Hooke peeked through his lens at cork and thought the tiny boxes looked like little rooms, naming them cells.

q: Which of the following is the MOST readily available energy store during normal human cellular conditions:
e: Inside your busy cells, ATP acts like instant pocket money, ready to spend the very second you need a burst of power!

q: Old growth forests and ancient cypress swamps would be examples of which of the following?
e: These grand ancient forests are cozy climax communities, where nature has finished growing and settled happily into a forever home.

q: Which of the following is the scientific name for the thigh bone:
e: Meet the mighty femur, the longest bone in your body that happily powers every jump and stomp from inside your thigh!

q: Which of the following is an example of a gymnosperm?
e: Ancient ginkgo trees are proud gymnosperms because their seeds grow right out in the open, without hiding inside sweet fruits or flowers.

q: Which of the following genetic disorders results from a chromosomal trisomy [TRY-soh-mee]?
e: Down syndrome happens when an extra chromosome joins the dance, making three copies instead of the usual two.

q: Which of the following is the phylum to which organisms with large amounts of chitin belong:
e: Arthropods like crabs and beetles wear awesome crunchy suits made of chitin, walking around in their own built-in armor!

q: Halophytes [HAIL-oh-fites] are plants that have adapted to which of the following environmental challenges?
e: Halophytes are brave little plant adventurers with special tricks for drinking salty water that would make ordinary plants shrivel up.

q: Which of the following anatomical structures do sharks NOT possess:
e: Unlike other fish wearing bony little gill covers, sharks let their open gill slits flap freely in the rushing sea.

q: Which of the following annelids has a sucker at each end of its body?
e: Leeches inch along like little acrobats because they have handy suction cups on both front and back ends to stick tight!

q: What are the scales on all snakes and most lizards are made of?
e: A snake wears a shiny suit of keratin, the exact same tough stuff found in your own fingernails.

q: Keratin and hemoglobin are both examples of which of the following macromolecules?
e: Whether giving your hair strength or zooming oxygen through your blood, keratin and hemoglobin are both hardworking proteins.

q: Human epidermis is MOSTLY composed of which of the following basic animal tissue types?
e: Your outer skin is mostly epithelial tissue, locking together like microscopic bricks to keep you safely wrapped up.

q: Which of the following is an example of metamorphosis?
a: A rabbit giving birth to eight young
A bumble bee larva forming a pupa and emerging as a mature adult
A baby bird emerging from the egg
A stink bug transitioning through multiple instars eventually becoming a mature adult
e: Metamorphosis is nature's ultimate costume change, like a squishy bee larva tucked in its pupa until it sprouts wings and buzzes out.

q: If you are looking at a specimen with a compound microscope using a 40X objective and a 10X eyepiece, what would be the total magnification?
e: The lenses team up by multiplying forty times ten, giving your curious eyes a super-view of 400 times bigger.

q: A nucleotide contains all except which of the following?
e: Amino acids belong to proteins, so DNA's tiny building blocks leave them out of their special three-part recipe.

q: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for the function of respiration?
e: Meet the mitochondrion, the tiny cellular powerhouse that breathes in oxygen to turn your food into pure, bouncing energy!

q: Sea sponges can have hearts.
e: Sea sponges live a very relaxed life without any hearts at all, happily letting ocean currents do all the pumping for them.

q: To what phylum [FYE- lum] does baker's yeast belong?
e: Baker's yeast belongs to the Ascomycota family, a cozy club of fungi that pack their tiny spores inside little microscopic sacs.

q: Gas exchange in human lungs primarily occurs between a network of capillaries and what structures with increased surface area?
e: Deep in your lungs, millions of balloon-like alveoli hug tiny blood vessels to trade fresh oxygen for tired old air.

q: Given typical environmental abundances, which would you expect to be MOST abundant in a drop of seawater?
e: In every single splash of ocean water, billions of tiny viruses easily outnumber all the other swimming microbes combined.

q: In healthy mammals, which of the following is least likely to be filtered out of the bloodstream by the glomerulus [glo-MAIR-yoo-lus]?
e: Albumin is like a giant beach ball, far too big to squeeze through the kidney's tiny filter holes! It stays happily inside your blood.

q: Which of the following is the role of DNA ligase [LY-gayz] in DNA replication?
a: Joining the 3' [3-prime] end of the DNA that replaces the primer to the rest of the sequence
Relieving strain caused by over-winding the DNA strand
e: Think of DNA ligase as molecular glue, neatly sealing loose ends together so the brand-new genetic strip stays unbroken.

q: Which of the following is NOT a protist?
e: While the others are all protists, Anabaena is actually a clever bacterium that links together like a glowing necklace.

q: A plasmid is a circular DNA molecule that is separate from chromosomal DNA, usually occurring in bacteria. Which of the following do plasmids usually contain?
e: Plasmids are tiny circles of DNA that travel light, usually holding just one or two handy bonus genes for a bacterium.

q: An ecologist notices that there are two distinct populations of sparrows that cannot interbreed due to infertility. This demonstrates which of the following types of isolation?
e: This is gametic isolation because their egg and sperm cells simply cannot join together to start new bird families.

q: Which of the following organelles regulates what enters and leaves the cell?
e: The cell membrane acts like a watchful bouncer at the door, deciding exactly what gets to enter or leave.

q: What is the largest terrestrial biome, characterized by large populations of coniferous [koh-NIH-fur-us] trees?
e: The chilly taiga stretches across the north like a giant green blanket, packed with millions of pointy cone-bearing trees.

q: During which of the following activities would you expect there to be the highest concentration of lactic acid in the leg muscles of a human?
e: When you sprint hard, your leg muscles run out of oxygen and quickly make lactic acid to keep you moving.

q: Which of the following do all chordates possess at some time in their lives:
e: Long before they grow up, all chordates share a secret badge of honor: tiny gill slits tucked along their necks!

q: Which of the following errors in human meiosis would LEAST likely affect the resulting offspring?
a: Gene duplication in a transcriptionally-silent region of the chromosome
Gene duplication in a transcriptionally-active region of the chromosome
e: Because that quiet part of the chromosome is sleeping and turned off, making extra copies causes no trouble at all.

q: During the summer months, which of the following plant structures is NOT a sugar sink?
e: In warm summer sunshine, busy leaves are bustling factories making sweet sugar for everyone else, not storing it for themselves.

q: In humans, chemical digestion of protein does NOT occur in which of the following areas?
e: Your mouth loves chomping food and breaking down sugars, but chemical protein digestion must wait until your stomach wakes up!

q: Which of the following is the hereditary material in most living things?
e: DNA is life's amazing recipe book, packed with inherited instructions passed down from parents to build wonderfully unique you!

q: During the Deep Water Horizon oil spill, marine microbes were observed to consume some of the released hydrocarbons. Which of the following crude oil components is most likely to be degraded quickly by marine microbes?
e: Ethane is tiny and simple, making it a quick, bite-sized snack that hungry microbes can gobble up in a snap.

q: Most biological catalysts are:
e: These hardworking little helpers that speed up your body's chemistry are almost always made of proteins folded into handy tools.

q: When using the gel electrophoresis technique, which of the following DNA segments will migrate the furthest from where they were loaded?
e: In this gooey obstacle race, the smallest DNA pieces easily slip through tiny spaces and zoom the farthest!

q: For an environment where a long-lasting toxin has been introduced, in which organism of a food chain will you expect to find the least accumulation of the toxin?
e: Plant producers sit at the very start of the food chain, so they collect the least poison since they never eat other creatures!

q: Baroreceptors in the human brain are responsible for monitoring which of the following quantities?
a: Position and stretching of smooth muscles
Relative position of the head with respect to gravity
e: Tiny baroreceptors act like little pressure gauges, feeling the gentle push of blood against your vessels to track blood pressure.

q: You find a new creature measuring over 4 millimeters in size in your bedroom. You notice that it has 6 legs so you know it is some type of:
e: Count those six wiggly little legs, and you will always know you are looking at an insect!

q: A liver cell is slowly dying because it can not break down toxins. What organelle is likely defective in this cell?
e: The endoplasmic reticulum is the liver cell's busy cleanup crew, scrubbing away harmful toxins to keep everything safe and sound.

q: Some plants have bacteria within their root nodules that perform nitrogen fixation. What conversion does nitrogen fixation involve?
e: Clever root bacteria grab floating dinitrogen gas from the air and turn it into tasty ammonia that plants can actually eat!

q: Which of the following animals completes a round-trip migration over several generations?
e: Tiny globe skimmer dragonflies treat migration like a family relay race, letting their children and grandchildren finish the epic round trip.

q: Kate is constructing a cladogram [KLAD-oh-gram] that includes angiosperms, conifers, ferns, and mosses. Which of the following is most likely to be an ancestral trait of this cladogram?
e: All these green plant buddies stand up tall using stems, an ancient trait they shared way before flowers or seeds ever appeared.

q: Which of the following ocean animals' eggs hatch at low tide?
e: Baby sea turtles wait under the warm sand until low tide, scurrying safely toward the ocean before the water rushes back in.

q: Which of the following is NOT a potential control mechanism for regulating gene expression in eukaryotic [yoo-KAR-ee-oh-tik] organisms?
a: The transport of mRNA from the nucleus
e: The lactose operon is a neat switchboard used only by simple bacteria, not by big, fancy eukaryotic cells.

q: Which of the major groups of plants contains no vasculature [VASS-kyu-lah-chur]?
e: Bryophytes like fuzzy mosses have no water pipes inside, so they stay tiny and soak up puddles like little green sponges.

q: Which of the following types of nucleic acid carries a complementary copy of a gene from the DNA to the cytoplasm to instruct the order in which amino acids will be made into a protein:
e: Messenger RNA acts like a cheerful mail carrier, delivering precious recipe copies from cozy DNA right out to the cell's protein kitchen!

q: Cell theory, one of the most fundamental principles of modern biology, consists of three main ideas. Which of the following is NOT one of cell theory's main ideas?
a: All organisms are composed of one or more cells
The cell is the basic unit of organization for organisms
All cells come from preexisting cells
e: Cell theory is all about how living things are built, so causing infectious disease was never invited to join its big rules.

q: ATP is commonly called the energy molecule of the cell. Where in the cell would you find ATP made by substrate phosphorylation?
e: Right in the cell's jelly-like cytoplasm, little enzymes quickly snap energy packets together to make handy ATP.

q: Which of the following is the botanical term for the haploid generation in moss plants:
e: That soft green carpet of moss in the woods is the gametophyte stage, proudly carrying one set of genes.

q: Which of the following is an example of a zoonotic [ZOH-uh-naw-tik] disease?
e: Bubonic plague is zoonotic because sneaky germs leaped from fleas riding on rats straight onto humans!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of earthworms reproduction:
a: the clitellum secretes a cocoon that picks up eggs and stored sperm
earthworm embryos develop inside the nephrostome (read as: neff-ro-stome) of the male
e: Baby worms actually grow inside cozy soil cocoons, not inside a nephrostome, which is just a fancy worm kidney!

q: Which of the following pairs of organisms best demonstrates the concept of mutualism?
e: Underground, mycorrhiza and plants trade water for sweet sugar, forming a wonderful friendship where both help each other thrive.

q: Bioluminescence is light originating in an organism that is produced by a chemical reaction. Which of the following statements is NOT true about bioluminescence?
a: It is the predominant source of light in the deep ocean
The luminescent wake of a ship is due to dinoflagellates (read as: dy-ne-FLAH-jeg-lehts)
Most marine bioluminescence is blue in color
All firefly species are bioluminescent as adults
e: Believe it or not, some grown-up fireflies actually prefer the dark, keeping their little lanterns turned off for good.

q: Which of the following represents the primary symptom from the chytrid fungus infecting amphibians?
a: The fungus attacks the skin, making respiration difficult
The fungal spores enter through the eyes, causing permanent blindness
The fungus is ingested and produces repeated regurgitation followed by death
e: Frogs need soft skin to breathe, so this unkind fungus thickens their outer coat until taking a breath becomes terribly hard.

q: What type of animal is a natterjack?
e: Meet the natterjack, a yellow-striped toad that scurries across sandy dunes on little legs instead of hopping!

q: Which of the following is the MAJOR difference between Lamarck's and Darwin's theories of evolution?
a: Lamarck's theory could be applied to giraffes
Lamarck's theory involves changes to a population
Darwin's theory involves changes to a population
Darwin's theory involves changes to an individual
e: Darwin realized that nature guides the whole team, meaning entire populations slowly change together across generations.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding chloroplasts?
a: Chloroplasts possess inner and outer membranes
Pigment molecules and proteins associate to form photosystems
The stroma is characterized by surface area-increasing folds called cristae [KRIS-tee]
e: Those wavy folds called cristae actually live inside mitochondria, so chloroplasts get to keep their own stroma smooth.

q: Which of the following is an adaptation in birds that facilitates flight?
e: To easily lift off into the sky, birds pack light with hollow bones that keep their bodies wonderfully weightless.

q: Which part of the body does glaucoma affect?
e: Glaucoma builds up sneaking pressure inside the eyes, threatening the wondrous windows you see the world with.

q: Which of the following cellular components is present in eukaryotes [YOO-care-ee-oats], but not prokaryotes [PRO-care-ee-oats]?
e: Eukaryote cells keep their precious DNA tucked safely inside a cozy little headquarters called a nucleus, while simpler prokaryotes let theirs float freely.

q: Which of the following would be considered an autotroph (read as: AW-toh-tref)?
e: An oak tree is an autotroph because it catches sunshine with green leaves to bake its own food from scratch!

q: What is a large community of plants and animals that live in the same place?
e: A biome is a giant ecological neighborhood where big communities of plants and creatures share the land and climate.

q: Sharks do not have a swim bladder. What major organ controls buoyancy in sharks?
e: A shark stays afloat with a giant liver packed with light, buoyant oil, like wearing built-in water wings!

q: "Decapods" are an order of ten-footed crustaceans.  Which of these are NOT decapods?
e: While lobsters strut on ten legs, tiny krill paddle through the sea with feathery swimming feet, so they aren't decapods!

q: If you put a bacterium with a plasmid for antibiotic resistance into a growth medium with antibiotic, virtually all of the population grown from the starting bacterium will have a copy of the plasmid. However, if you take the same starting bacterium and put it in a growth medium without an antibiotic, many of the progeny will NOT have a copy of the plasmid. Which of the following is the BEST explanation for this observation?
a: Plasmids can be transferred from one bacterium to another
Plasmids have to be beneficial to be replicated
Plasmids are permanent in a population
e: Carrying extra DNA costs energy, so bacteria only keep their helpful plasmids when they truly need them to survive.

q: Which of the following terms is used by microbiologists to describe a bacterium with a rod shape?
e: When scientists spot a tiny bacterium shaped like a little hot dog or rod, they politely call it a bacillus.

q: The crop plants kohlrabi, kale, cabbage, Brussels sprouts, broccoli, and cauliflower are all human cultivars of the wild mustard plant. Which of the following best describes the process by which these modern plants came into existence?
e: Creative farmers used artificial selection, handpicking their favorite wild mustard traits over years to cook up broccoli and cabbage!

q: Which of the following neurotransmitters is NOT generally inhibitory?
e: While other brain messengers whisper for quiet, peppy glutamate excites nerve cells and tells them to fire away!

q: Which of the following best describes antibodies:
a: a class of polysaccharides involved in the immune system
a group of proteins made by plasma cells in response to a foreign substance
small bodies of insects that look like ants
a class of genes produced by the immune system to fight disease
e: Antibodies are clever little proteins made by plasma cells, rushing out like tiny bodyguards to tag unwelcome germ invaders.

q: In the tri-nomen Canis lupis familiaris, Canis refers to what taxonomic rank?
e: Canis is the genus, a proud group name that packs wolves, jackals, and our favorite pet dogs together like close cousins.

q: Which of the following is the male reproductive part of a flower?
e: Meet the stamen, the flower's pollen-making boy part standing tall to dust visiting bees with golden grains!

q: In what cellular component does a plant cell store water?
e: Think of the central vacuole as a giant, thirsty water balloon inside the plant cell, keeping everything fresh and crisp.

q: An intracellular substance is so named because it is located in which of the following places:
e: Think of "intra" as staying indoors; an intracellular substance lives cozy and tucked away right within the cell's tiny walls.

q: When two species compete for the same resources and one species is eliminated, the outcome is referred to as which of the following?
e: When two critters chase the exact same snack, the winner completely excludes the loser, kicking them out through competitive exclusion.

q: In human nerves, the nerve impulse or message occurs primarily because of the movement of ions of what two elements across the cell membranes of nerves:
e: Tiny sodium and potassium particles dance across cell doorways, passing tiny sparks to send messages through your nerves.

q: Which of the following mammals has the greatest diploid number of chromosomes?
e: You might expect an elephant to win, but the little aquatic rat carries the biggest bundle of chromosome instructions in this furry lineup.

q: A biologist wants to test the effect of a new food additive on growth in rats. An experimental group was fed a diet containing the additive. Which of the following would be an effective control group?
a: A group of rats that ate a higher concentration of food additive
A group of rats that were kept in different conditions across the city
A group of rats that were fed the same ration without the food additive
A group of rats that ate a lower concentration of the food additive
e: To see if the additive really works, you need buddy rats eating the exact same meal without it to compare against!

q: Which of the following best describes a karyotype (read as: KAH-ree-oh-typ)?
a: A region of the chromosome where the two sister chromatids are held together
An organized visual profile of the chromosomes
Chromosomes found in mitochondria (read as: my-toh-KOHN-dree-ah) and chloroplasts
e: A karyotype is like school picture day for chromosomes, neatly lining them up so scientists have an organized photo profile to study!

q: Which of the following is involved in a frameshift DNA mutation?
a: Part of one chromosome breaking off and attaching to another chromosome
A segment of a chromosome is repeated at least once
The insertion or deletion of a nucleotide in the coding sequence of a gene
Only a single point in the DNA sequence
e: Adding or deleting a single gene letter shifts the entire reading frame, scrambling every word in the recipe that comes next.

q: Which of the following is an example of a frameshift mutation?
a: Adding one nucleotide in the middle of a gene
Deleting three nucleotides in the middle of a gene
Adding three nucleotides in the middle of a gene
e: Slipping a single extra letter into the gene scrambles every three-letter word after it, shifting the whole recipe out of line.

q: Which of the following animals has the longest gestation period?
e: Mother elephants carry their gigantic, cuddly calves for nearly two whole years before welcoming them into the sunny world.

q: The kingdom Plantae [PLAN-tee] consists of members that are which of the following?
e: Plants are bustling neighborhoods of complex eukaryotic cells, teaming up to catch golden sunshine and make their own delicious food.

q: Which of the following hormones induces glucose uptake by cells after food consumption?
e: After you eat, insulin acts like a friendly doorman, unlocking your cells so sweet sugar can step inside and fuel you up.

q: The human genome has been mapped. In this mapping process, they identified genes that coded for all of the following, except:
e: Our DNA codes for traits like hair color and vision, but race is a social idea, not a single gene you can find.

q: Which of the following is the role of DNA ligase in DNA replication?
a: Joining the 3 prime end of the DNA that replaces the primer to the rest of the sequence
Relieving strain caused by over-winding the DNA strand
e: DNA ligase acts like molecular tape, neatly gluing the newly replaced DNA ends right into the matching genetic strand.

q: Which of the following do chloroplasts have in common with mitochondria (read as: my-toh-KOHN-dree-ah)?
a: They do not contain ribosomes (read as: RY-boh-sems)
They replicate themselves and their own DNA
e: These two tiny power-makers act like independent helpers, carrying their own special DNA and copying themselves whenever the cell needs more!

q: Which of the following events would lead to increased diversity in a population?
e: A mutation is nature's surprise artist, shuffling the genetic deck to introduce brand new traits that make a population wonderfully diverse!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of an angiosperm [AN-jee-uh-spurm]?
e: Douglas firs make woody pinecones instead of flowers and fruit, which means they are gymnosperms, not angiosperms.

q: Which of the following cellular organelles is responsible for energy production in the eukaryotic cell?
e: The mighty mitochondrion is the cell's roaring little power plant, busily turning food into bright bursts of usable energy.

q: Differentiation of cells during plant development is MOST commonly associated with:
a: allowing cells to recognize other cells
e: As plant cells grow up, differentiation lets them choose their dream job, maturing into specialized workers like roots or colorful petals!

q: "Tachycardia" or "Tachyarrhythmia" refers to a resting heart-rate near or over 100 BPM.
e: It is true, because tachycardia means your resting heart is zipping along at a super-fast speed of one hundred beats each minute!

q: Which of the following is closest to the meaning of intercellular (read carefully as: in-TER-cellular):
e: Just like an interstate connects different cities, "intercellular" means anything hanging out in the cozy spaces between neighboring cells.

q: Which of the following magnifications is most appropriate for viewing bacteria through a light microscope?
e: Teeny bacteria need a big zoom to reveal their secrets, and five hundred times lets a regular light microscope show them clearly!

q: Which of the following types of trees includes individuals that were saplings when the great pyramids were built and are still alive today?
e: High on windy mountaintops, ancient bristlecone pines have quietly stood watch for thousands of years, living long before the pyramids were finished!

q: Most animal eukaryotic cells have:
a: a cell wall, nucleus, and cytoplasm
a plasma membrane, nucleus, and cytoplasm
a cell wall, nucleus, and nucleolus
a cell wall, nucleus, and mitochondrion
e: Animal cells are squishy, wrapping their control-center nucleus and jelly-like cytoplasm inside a flexible plasma membrane instead of a rigid wall.

q: Which of the following is a relatively short fragment of DNA created on the lagging strand during DNA replication?
e: Copying DNA backward in little hops, the cell stitches together short puzzle pieces called Okazaki fragments.

q: The cardiac center is located in which of the following structures?
e: Tucked at the brain's base, the marvelous medulla quietly works day and night to keep your beating heart on beat.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the black-footed ferret?
a: They like to eat prairie dogs
They neared total extinction in the 1980s
They like to live in groups
They have one to six young in a litter
e: These sneaky, masked critters are solitary homebodies who prefer living all alone in their burrows instead of hanging out in groups.

q: A farmer has planted corn in a field for the last 5 years, and has been disappointed with his crop yield for the last 2 years. Which of the following crops should he plant next year to maximize the corn yield for the following year?
a: Nothing, it will let the soil recover completely from being planted
Potatoes, because they have the deepest roots and will aerate the soil
Peas, because they will maximize the nitrogen in the soil for the corn
Wheat, because they use different nutrients than the corn
e: Friendly peas share a secret superpower: they team up with soil microbes to pack the dirt with nitrogen for next year's hungry corn!

q: In comparison to sexual reproduction, asexual reproduction produces which of the following?
e: By simply copying one parent, asexual reproduction makes identical copies of life, meaning there is far less genetic variety in the family.

q: The skull of a new mammalian species is found and all of the teeth are sharp and angled. Based on this data, which of the following is the most reasonable conclusion?
e: Those dagger-sharp teeth were made for slicing meat, proving this creature was definitely a hungry carnivore.

q: A mutant fly is observed with an antenna growing out of the abdomen, rather than the head. Which of the following gene types is most likely involved in this kind of mutation?
e: Homeotic genes are the body's master builders. When they get mixed up, they might accidentally stick an antenna right on a fly's tummy!

q: Which of the following animals has the highest osmolarity in their extracellular fluids?
e: Swimming in the salty deep ocean, squids keep their body fluids extra salty to match the sea around them.

q: Having a single ventricle limits oxygen delivery for a three- chambered heart. Which of the following animals has a three-chambered heart?
e: Frogs hop to the beat of an unusual three-chambered heart, sharing just one main pumping room inside their chest.

q: Cashmere is the wool from which kind of animal?
e: That cloud-soft cashmere sweater actually comes from the warm, fluffy undercoat of mountain goats keeping cozy in chilly winds.

q: Which of the following species thrives in a mangrove?
e: Mighty alligators love swampy mangroves, gliding smoothly through the warm, tangled tree roots on the hunt.

q: Which of the following groups are all invertebrates?
a: Snails, honeybees, sea star, and sea sponges
Grasshoppers, fruit flies, electric eels, and sea horses
e: From squishy snails and bees to sea stars and sponges, none of these little friends have a single backbone!

q: The wing of a bird and the arm of a human are considered:
e: Bird wings and human arms are homologous structures because they share the very same ancient bone blueprint, just built for different adventures!

q: Which of the following structures is reponsible for maintaining homeostasis [home-ee-oh-STAY-sis] in humans?
e: The hypothalamus acts like your body's cozy thermostat, keeping your temperature and balance happy through a superpower called homeostasis.

q: Base substitutions that occur in coding regions that result in the change from one amino acid to another in the resulting protein are referred to as what type of mutation?
e: In a missense mutation, swapping just one tiny letter accidentally tells the cell to build with a completely different amino acid recipe piece.

q: In Alzheimer's disease, which of the following brain regions shows the first signs of protein aggregation?
e: The brain's memory scrapbook begins in the hippocampus, where the CA1 section sadly shows the very first signs of sticky protein tangles.

q: Which of the following groups of animals is able to respire significant amounts of oxygen from their skins?
e: Amphibians have moist, magical skin that lets them breathe fresh oxygen straight from the air and water around them!

q: What makes the phosphorus cycle unique from the nitrogen, carbon, or oxygen cycles?
a: It only occurs in rocks or soils
It does not significantly involve the atmosphere
e: While other elements love soaring through the airy sky, shy phosphorus stays grounded, happily skipping the atmosphere to travel through rocks and soil instead.

q: Which of the following organisms has most of its genes organized into operons?
e: Tiny bacteria like E. coli pack their genes into tidy little teams called operons, letting them switch jobs on together in a snap!

q: Which of the following characteristics will a lake that has undergone eutrophication exhibit [yoo-tro-fi-KAY-shun]?
a: The lake will be clear and cold
The lake will be high in nutrients
The lake will support large numbers of fish
The lake will have low primary productivity
e: Think of eutrophication as a lake eating way too much plant food, getting super stuffed with extra nutrients until green algae takes over!

q: Otters have pockets under their arms for carrying their favourite snacks and rocks.
e: Believe it or not, otters really do have loose skin folds under their arms that act as pockets for their favorite pebbles!

q: A biologist identifies a new unicellular species lacking a nucleus that can undergo both transcription and translation concurrently on the same strand of mRNA. Which of the following groups of organisms could this cell be a member of?
e: Without a nucleus wall in the way, busy bacteria can read gene recipes and cook up proteins all at once!

q: Which of the following scenarios is an example of Brownian motion?
a: Certain molecules diffusing across a cellular membrane
Unicellular organisms moving through water by the propulsion of flagella
Active transport of molecules across a cellular membrane
e: Molecules love to wiggle and bump randomly into their neighbors, dancing their way across cell membranes like bumper cars.

q: If you eat a tuna fish sandwich, which of the following types of fish would you be eating?
e: Tuna zoom through the water with fins supported by webs of tiny bony rods, making them super-fast ray-finned fish!

q: Passive transport differs mostly from active transport since passive transport requires:
e: Passive transport is like coasting effortlessly down a playground slide, requiring absolutely no energy to slip right through the door.

q: Which of the following is the porcupine's primary mode of defense from predators?
e: Porcupines protect themselves with sharp, barbed quills that hook easily into curious sniffers and stubbornly refuse to let go.

q: What is the net ATP gain of glycolysis?
e: Sugar-breaking spends two energy coins and makes four, proudly handing your cell a cozy net profit of just two ATP.

q: A geneticist breeds two pea plants that are heterozygous for seed color. Given that 2001 of the F2 generation are homozygous recessive, which of the following is closest to the number of plants that exhibit the dominant trait?
e: For every quiet plant showing the hidden trait, three proud plants show the dominant one, giving us about 6,006 colorful sprouts!

q: Which of the following organisms is most closely related to sharks, rays, and skates?
e: Built from bendy cartilage instead of hard bone, the mysterious chimaera is a swimming cousin to sharks and rays.

q: Antibodies are composed of:
e: These tiny shield-shaped superhero proteins are built by stringing together trusty little building blocks called amino acids.

q: Which of the following is a common excitatory neurotransmitter in mammals:
e: Acetylcholine acts like an eager messenger inside you, happily shouting 'wake up and move' to get your hard-working muscles dancing.

q: What environmental condition is mandatory for yeast to complete fermentation?
e: Yeast only kicks off its bubbling fermentation magic when there is zero oxygen around for it to breathe.

q: In what part of the digestive tract are nutrients primarily absorbed into the bloodstream?
e: With its long, velvety walls, the small intestine acts like a hungry sponge, soaking up precious food nutrients right into your blood.

q: The presence of which of the following is what makes rough endoplasmic reticulum appear rough and not smooth?
e: Tiny protein-making dots called ribosomes speckle the surface like bumpy sprinkles, making this cellular helper look totally rough.

q: Which of the following is the term for a plant that can be found living on top of another plant but which obtains its nutrients and water independently?
e: An epiphyte politely perches high on a tree branch to catch fresh rain, living independently without stealing any food from its neighbor.

q: Microscopic zooplankton [ZOH-oh-plank-ton] can best be classified as which of the following trophic levels?
e: These tiny ocean wanderers are herbivores, happily grazing on microscopic green plants drifting in the sea.

q: When your body tissues need more calcium, what endocrine structure is activated to signal the release of more calcium into your blood?
e: Tiny parathyroid glands act like watchful lifeguards, releasing a chemical alarm to send stored calcium rushing back into your bloodstream.

q: Which of the following is an example of chemosynthesis?
a: A Venus flytrap breaking down the phosphates in a fly
A plant obtaining fixated nitrogen from bacteria rich soil
Prokaryotes [proh-KAR-ee-ohts] obtaining energy from sulfur compounds from the sea vents on the ocean floor
A human being breaking down vitamins and minerals for metabolic digestion
e: Deep in the pitch-black ocean, tiny microbes make chemosynthesis magic by turning harsh vent chemicals into tasty meals without sunlight.

q: Which of the following does NOT occur during prometaphase [pro- MEHTA-phase]?
a: Chromatids [CROW-mah-tids] arrive at opposite cell poles
Kinetochores [kin-EHT-oh-cores] form as proteins attached to centromeres [SEN-troh-meers]
e: The twin chromatids are still getting ready to dance, saving their big trip to opposite poles for much later in the show!

q: Aerobic organisms fuel their metabolism by reducing molecular oxygen through respiration. Some organisms are able to undergo anaerobic respiration, where another oxidized molecule is substituted for oxygen. Which of the following would be a good substitute for oxygen in anaerobic respiration?
e: When fresh oxygen is missing, clever mud microbes breathe in sulfate instead to keep their engines running.

q: Which of the following membrane-bounded vesicles contains hydrolytic enzymes used for intracellular digestion?
e: Meet the lysosome, the cell's tidy little stomach that uses digestive juices to gobble up old clutter!

q: In addition to being birds, what do the Great Auk, moa, passenger pigeon, and Carolina parakeet have in common?
a: They are all listed as invasive species in North America
They are all listed as threatened species in their native habitats
They are all being raised in captive breeding programs for later release into the wild
e: Sadly, these magnificent feathered friends are extinct, meaning every single one has vanished from our world forever.

q: Another bacterium living in the mud utilizes the hydrogen sulfide in its own metabolism. What molecule is it most likely to use in a redox reaction with hydrogen sulfide?
e: Hungry mud microbes love pairing up smelly hydrogen sulfide with nitrate to zap out energy and power their day.

q: After a forest fire, what specific type of succession rebuilds the ecosystem?
e: Because healthy soil stays behind after the flames, the forest can rebuild itself through secondary succession.

q: Which of the following is the best description of a cell membrane also known as the plasma membrane?
a: it is permeable and made of mostly proteins
it is semi-permeable and made mostly of proteins in a lipid bilayer
it is impermeable and made up mostly of lipids
it is a fluid mosaic composed of a protein bilayer
e: This membrane is a semi-permeable lipid bilayer loaded with proteins, acting like a picky gatekeeper that lets special goodies pass.

q: Which of the following is part of the nephron in the kidney:
e: Deep inside your kidney nephron, a tiny tangled ball called the glomerulus filters your blood like a magical sieve!

q: Which of the following biomes has the lowest net primary production?
e: The icy tundra is so bitterly cold that plants barely grow, leaving it with the lowest biological production.

q: What part of the brain plays a major role in endocrine [EN-doh-krin] regulation, and is primarily responsible for maintaining homeostasis?
e: The hypothalamus is your brain's master thermostat, balancing your whole body by bossing around your hormone glands.

q: What dog breed is one of the oldest breeds of dog and has flourished since before 400 BCE.
e: With their cute wrinkled faces, charming pugs were already beloved royal lapdogs over two thousand years ago!

q: Which of the following marine organisms would be considered ectothermic?
e: A sea turtle is ectothermic, so this scaly swimmer relies on the warm sunshine and water to heat up!

q: Which of the following is a protein:
e: Trypsin is a hardworking protein enzyme, snapping apart food proteins in your gut like a tiny pair of scissors.

q: Which of the following does not demonstrate external radial symmetry?
e: Round sea anemones spread out like bicycle wheels, but wiggly eels have matching left and right sides instead.

q: The medical condition osteoporosis affects which part of the body?
e: This condition quietly sneaks inside your bones, turning a sturdy skeleton brittle and weak.

q: The first prokaryotes [proh-KAR-ee-ohts], eukaryotes [yoo-KAR-ee-ohts], and multicellular organisms all arose during which of the following evolutionary eras?
e: Way back in the ancient Precambrian era, life first sparked, growing from lonely single cells into complex multicellular teams.

q: What is the fastest animal?
e: When this feathered daredevil folds its wings and dives, the peregrine falcon zooms faster than a racecar, beating every creature on Earth.

q: Bacteria are more likely used to produce which of the following:
e: Tiny, hardworking bacteria happily gobble up alcohol and turn it into the tangy, sour vinegar we splash on salads!

q: Which of the following types of interactions will NOT occur between enzymes and their substrates?
e: Enzymes hold their helpers with soft, temporary hugs rather than strong covalent bonds, so they can let go easily.

q: Parasitic flatworms, commonly called flukes, that infect the internal organs of their hosts are in which of the following classes?
e: Flukes belong to Trematoda, a group of sneaky flatworms that love setting up camp deep inside an animal's organs.

q: Which of the following is NOT a baleen whale?
e: While baleen whales use giant hairy strainers to catch snacks, pilot whales smile with a mouth full of real teeth!

q: The dish Fugu, is made from what family of fish?
e: Chefs prepare fugu from the spiky pufferfish, carefully slicing away danger so brave diners can taste this famous round swimmer!

q: Because DNA polymerase (read as: poh-LIM-eh-rayz) is not able to synthesize DNA in the 3 prime to the 5 prime direction, how do eukaryotes (read as: yuh-KEHR-ee-ets) prevent loss of base pair sequences from chromosome ends?
a: Topoisomerase (read as: te-pe-y-SOH-meh-rayz) winds up DNA ends
Telomerase (read as: te-LE-meh-rayz) adds sequence repeats
e: Telomerase acts like a tiny knitter, adding extra repeating caps to chromosome ends so important instructions never get lost.

q: The human ABO blood group system is an example of which of the following?
e: In co-dominance, blood types A and B share the spotlight equally, happily working side by side without either one bossing the other around.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method by which speciation is known to occur?
a: A group of similar animals moves to a new landmass with no natural predators
A busy highway is built through a forest
A predator randomly selects animals from a prey population to consume
Chromosome ploidy changes during plant reproduction
e: A hungry hunter snacking at random just fills its belly. It never separates animals enough to make a brand-new species!

q: Which of the following environmental limits on population growth is density-independent?
e: Wild weather doesn't care how crowded a forest gets; a chilly snowstorm treats one lonely squirrel the same as fifty!

q: Which color cannot be produced in Roses, even through genetic alteration?
e: Roses simply lack the natural blue recipe in their genes, so a true blue petal stays pure fairytale magic.

q: The structure of DNA proposed by Watson and Crick was partly based on the x-ray work of:
e: Brilliant scientist Rosalind Franklin captured the famous, dazzling X-ray photograph that revealed DNA's gorgeous twisting spiral ladder.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the plant Mimosa pudica [mee-MO-suh POO-dee-kuh]?
a: Its leaves fold inward and droop when it is touched or shaken
Aqueous [AY-kwee-uhs] extracts of its roots inhibit cobra venom
e: This shy little plant actually began its journey in the Americas, not Africa, where it first learned to fold up its leaves.

q: Which of the following organisms is NOT a habitual biped?
e: Big-nosed proboscis monkeys love scampering on all four limbs through the trees, while true habitual bipeds stroll everywhere on two legs.

q: Which of the following cell types would be most important for an allergy response?
e: Basophils sound the alarm during allergies, releasing chemicals that make your nose tickle and sneeze!

q: Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis is a synonym for the disease known as silicosis.
e: That monster of a word is just a fancy name for silicosis, caused by breathing fine volcanic dust.

q: Which of the following energy conversions takes place during photosynthesis?
a: Light energy to mechanical energy to chemical energy
e: Leaves catch bright sunbeams and bake them into sweet, sugary fuel, turning light energy straight into chemical energy.

q: Which of the following types of feather helps birds maintain a constant body temperature?
e: Fluffy down feathers trap cozy pockets of warm air, acting like a bird's very own built-in winter puffy jacket!

q: Which of the following is the name for the blood cell in humans that plays the most central role in regulating the immune system:
e: Lymphocytes are the clever little generals of your bloodstream, directing your body's immune defenders to stop pesky invaders.

q: In humans, freely hanging earlobes is completely dominant to attached earlobes. If you have attached earlobes but both of your biological parents have freely hanging earlobes, then which of the following statements is true?
a: At least one of your parents is homozygous [hoh-muh-ZY-guhs] for the dominant trait
Both of your parents must be homozygous for the dominant trait
Neither of your parents is homozygous for the dominant trait
Nothing can be said about the genotype of your parents because there is not enough information
e: To give you attached earlobes, both parents must secretly carry that hidden gene, meaning neither is homozygous for the dominant trait.

q: What system in a mammalian body is responsible for removing liquids and solid wastes?
e: The excretory system is your body's trusty cleanup crew, whisking away leftover liquids and wastes to keep you clean inside.

q: Which of these organisms in not a kind of worm?
e: With dozens of scampering jointed legs and a crunchy outer shell, a centipede is an arthropod, not a squishy worm!

q: An individual with the monosomy [MAW-no-soh-mee] Turner syndrome has what karyotype [KAIR-ee-oh-type]?
e: Turner syndrome happens when someone has the X-O pattern, meaning they were born with a single X chromosome instead of two.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of genes:
a: they are a passed from generation to generation through chromosomes
they can come in dominant or recessive forms
genes often lead to the production of a protein
most of the DNA sequences in chromosomes are genes
e: Most of our DNA isn't genes at all, but quiet spaces, so actual genes are rare little treasures.

q: Which of the following parts of a fish can be used to estimate its age?
e: Just like tree trunks, a fish's scales grow tiny rings each year that reveal its secret age.

q: Which of the following plant phyla [FYE-lah] has the most extant species?
e: Anthophyta, the dazzling flowering plants, throw the biggest party on Earth with more buzzing species than any other plant family.

q: Which of the following types of plants is considered non-vascular?
e: Tiny mosses have no water pipes inside, so they hug the damp ground like fuzzy, thirsty little green sponges.

q: In eukaryotic cells, where does cellular respiration take place?
e: Mitochondria are the cell's bustling power plants, using cellular respiration to turn yummy food into pure, energetic fuel.

q: What organ in the human body is responsible for storing glucose in the form of glycogen?
e: Think of your liver as a cozy pantry, neatly packing away sugary snacks as glycogen until your body needs a boost!

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the events that occurs during translation?
e: Binding to a promoter happens way earlier when copying DNA, long before the cell's builders start translating recipes into proteins.

q: Which of the following animals are believed to be the closest living relatives to the dinosaurs:
e: Crocodiles and dinosaurs share the same ancient reptile family branch, making these toothy river giants their closest cousins alive today.

q: Fruit flies are common in homes, restaurants, supermarkets and wherever else fruit is allowed to rot and ferment. Given the opportunity, about how many eggs will a fruit fly lay at a time?
e: One busy little mother fruit fly can fill ripe fruit with about five hundred tiny future babies!

q: The Ceratosaurus, a dinosaur known for having a horn on the top of its nose, is also known to be a decendent of the Tyrannosaurus Rex.
e: That is false! Ceratosaurus actually stomped around millions of years before T. rex ever arrived on the scene.

q: The receptors in the retina of the eye that detect faint light and transfer non-color impulses to the brain are:
e: Night-vision superhero cells called rods help your eyes spot shadowy shapes when the lights go down low!

q: Which of the following was a top predator during the Devonian period?
e: Dunkleosteus was a mighty ancient fish wearing heavy armor that ruled Devonian seas like a giant underwater king with bone-snapping jaws!

q: Which of the following is the name of a highly contagious skin infection that mainly affects infants and children, appearing primarily as red sores on the face?
e: Impetigo is a sneaky skin bug that loves hopping between kids, leaving crusty red sores on little faces.

q: Muscle, connective, nerve, and epithelial are four basic types of animal:
e: When specialized cells team up like threads weaving together a warm blanket, they form these four basic types of body tissues.

q: Which of the following taxonomic categories is the highest rank, including all of the other choices?
e: Phylum is like a gigantic family umbrella, big enough to shelter whole classes, orders, and species all together.

q: What is the name of the family that the domestic cat is a member of?
e: Every purring pet cat belongs to Felidae, the grand family tree that also includes mighty lions and speedy cheetahs!

q: A biologist observes that different species of mice have different species of flea parasites. Which term best describes this scenario?
e: As the mice changed over time, their picky flea buddies changed right alongside them in a long evolutionary dance called coevolution.

q: Male pandas do handstands while urinating on trees.
e: It is true! Male pandas do acrobatic handstands on tree trunks so their smelly scent marks reach high into the breeze.

q: Which of the following cells can be described as totipotent [tow-TIH-puh-tent]?
e: A zygote is a magical fresh start, packed with the superpower to grow into every single part of a brand-new body.

q: A hospital technician centrifuges a vial of blood and notices a very thin milky white layer between two large layers. What can be found in these layers?
e: That milky white stripe is packed with leukocytes, our body's brave little white-blood-cell defenders taking a well-deserved rest.

q: The green pigment in plants that captures the energy of sunlight and initiates photosynthesis is called:
e: Chlorophyll is the plant's green solar panel, soaking up bright sunshine to help turn light into food.

q: "Kamea," the Gilbertese Islander word for dog, is derived from the English phrase "Come here!"
e: Pups eagerly ran whenever sailors shouted 'Come here,' so islanders turned that friendly call into their word for dog.

q: What is the most important function of fiber tracheids (read as: TRAY-key-ids) in woody plants:
a: absorption of nutrients from the soil
e: Think of fiber tracheids as a tree's tiny wooden bones, standing strong to give the plant support so it never falls over!

q: Strawberry plants can often be found with runners or stolons. Which of the following is the primary purpose of these structures?
e: Strawberry runners stretch out along the soil to sprout baby plant clones, making new families through asexual reproduction.

q: The nucleolus is the primary site for the manufacture of which of the following?
e: Deep inside the cell, the busy nucleolus works like a cozy factory, assembling tiny ribosomes to help build the rest of your body.

q: To which of the following virus classes does HIV belong?
e: HIV is a retrovirus because it works backward, turning its genetic recipe upside down to sneak into healthy cells.

q: What is the protein that binds nuclear material in DNA?
e: Histones act like tidy little spools, letting long threads of DNA wrap snugly around them to fit inside the nucleus.

q: What are the smallest blood vessels in the human body?
e: Capillaries are so wonderfully tiny that red blood cells must march through them in a single-file line!
