q: Transgenic animals carry the genes from other species in their DNA through a deliberate modification of their genome. Which of the following phrases does NOT reflect why transgenic animals are currently being produced in the United States?
a: To have animal models for human diseases
To test the purity of human proteins (such as human insulin) used as drugs
For the production of human food
e: While transgenic critters help scientists test medicines and study diseases, they are not made to fill our dinner plates with food.

q: Which of the following organisms has a hydrostatic skeleton?
e: Without hard bones inside, a sea star relies on water pressure trapped within its body to hold its shape and crawl.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of ribososmes:
a: they help translate mRNA into protein
they are too small to be seen with a compound light microscope
they are about 20 nanometers in diameter
bacterial and eukaryotic ribosomes are identical in shape and size
e: Ribosomes in bacteria and bigger creatures are not identical twins, because tiny bacterial builders make theirs in a smaller size.

q: Which of the following is an ectoparasite:
e: Sneaky lice are ectoparasites because they live on the outside of your body, clinging right to hair!

q: Which of the following elements is responsible for stimulating muscle contractions?
e: Calcium gives your muscle fibers a friendly tap on the shoulder, telling them it is time to squeeze together and flex!

q: Which of the following is NOT an illness caused by bacteria?
e: The sneaky flu is actually caused by a tiny virus, not a bacterium, when it brings on those chilly sneezes.

q: Which is NOT one of the essential activities that occurs in the digestive process?
e: Your tummy absorbs nutrients inside, but adsorption just means sticking to an outside surface, so it is not part of digestion.

q: Which of the following can prevent cell desiccation [des-i- KAY-shuhn] due to the osmotic pressure?
e: Tiny sodium channels act like clever little gates, letting salt in to keep thirsty cells plump and full of water.

q: You are using a light microscope to look at cells stained with a dye that detects chromatin [KROH-mah-tin] and can see densely-colored regions that you recognize as chromosomes. Which of the following must be true?
e: DNA only packs into tidy, visible chromosome bundles when a cell is ready to divide in mitosis!

q: Which of the following is a feeding structure in arachnids:
e: Spiders use chelicerae like tiny, built-in forks and fangs to grab and munch their tasty insect snacks.

q: The seed coat of angiosperm seeds typically develops from which of the following?
e: The plant wraps its tiny baby in protective layers called integuments, which toughen up into a snug little coat.

q: Which of the following is the location of the biceps humoris muscle:
e: When you proudly flex to show your strength, that big muscle popping up in your arm is your biceps.

q: Which of the following can NOT be classified in the class Cephalopoda [sef-uh-luh-POD-uh]?
e: While clever squids zoom with tentacles, the colorful nudibranch is actually a sea slug creeping along on its belly.

q: Which of the following parts of the cytoskeleton is involved in moving chromosomes during cell division?
e: Microtubules act like bustling microscopic ropes, gently pulling chromosomes apart so one cell can become two.

q: Which of the following is most likely to be true of a sessile animal?
e: Glued in one spot forever, a sessile creature simply sifts drifting snacks from passing water, making it a filter feeder.

q: Which of the following organisms has radial symmetry?
e: Round like a spiky little pincushion, a sea urchin can be sliced like a pizza and look the same from every side.

q: In which of the following cell types of woody higher plants is lignin most prominent:
e: Tough xylem tubes pack lots of woody lignin inside, helping trees stand tall and strong like mighty skyscrapers.

q: Which of the following is the primary reason for a cell to undergo arrest at the G2-M checkpoint of the cell cycle?
a: Chromosomes not attached to spindle fibers
e: A careful cell slams on the brakes if its precious DNA instruction book is missing pages and not fully copied yet.

q: Ribosomes [RYE-beh-sohms] produce numerous proteins needed for cellular functions. In what organelle can you find embedded ribosomes?
e: The rough endoplasmic reticulum gets its bumpy name because it is covered in bustling little protein makers called ribosomes.

q: What is the joint that is formed by the direct interaction of the tibia, fibula, and femur?
e: Your knee is the busy joint where your big thigh bone meets your two shin bones to help you bend.

q: Which of the following is NOT part of a prokaryotic (read as: pre-kahr-ee-AH-tik) cell?
e: Tiny prokaryotes love living simply, letting their genetic blueprints float freely without a cozy nucleus room to lock them inside.

q: What organelle in the cell contains enzymes for digestion?
e: Think of the lysosome as a hungry little tummy, using digestive juices to break down leftovers and tidy up the cell.

q: Indicate which of the following is most efficient for water and mineral transport in plants?
e: Vessel elements connect like wide, open drinking straws, letting water whoosh to thirsty leaves faster than any other plant pipe.

q: Which of the following is the most likely highest power for an objective lens on a typical student compound light microscope:
e: A 100-times lens is the strongest regular glass eye on a student microscope, zooming into tiny worlds without crashing slides.

q: In humans, red-green color blindness is caused by a recessive sex-linked trait on the X chromosome. If a man and a woman produce a color blind son, assuming no spontaneous mutation, which of the following must be true?
a: Both parents carry the allele for color blindness
The mother carries the allele for color blindness
Neither parent carries the allele for color blindness
e: A boy gets his Y chromosome from his dad, so that hidden color-blind X could only come from his mother.

q: On the Galapagos Islands, Darwin discovered 13 species of finches that possess specialized beaks for unique environments. Which of the following evolutionary principles is exemplified by this phenomenon?
e: Through adaptive radiation, one bird family branched into many new species, each sporting a beak shaped for its favorite island snack!

q: Which of the following is NOT a nucleic [new-CLAY-ik] acid?
e: DNA and RNA are the true genetic rulebooks of life, while DNR is just a hospital form and not a nucleic acid.

q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between epiphytes and the trees they live on?
e: In commensalism, epiphytes perch happily on tree branches to catch sunlight without bothering or harming their hosts at all.

q: Which of the following pairs of structures both contain linear DNA?
a: Animal cell nucleus and plant cell nucleus
e: Deep inside both plant and animal cells, their nuclei keep life's instructions neatly organized in long, straight strands of linear DNA.

q: Which of the following traits is NOT a characteristic of modern birds?
e: Birds need tons of power to soar through the sky, so their hearts have four hard-working chambers instead of three!

q: Somatic mutations are which of the following?
e: Somatic mutations are changes you acquire during your own adventures in life, instead of inheriting them from your parents!

q: Which of the following best describes a thallus?
a: A cellular connective structure found only in mammals
A plant-like body consisting of undifferentiated tissue
A process that bacteria undergo when infecting a host
A small rodent found only in Australia
e: A thallus is a simple, plant-like body made of undifferentiated tissue, happily growing without separate roots, stems, or leaves.

q: What is the organ system that delivers hormones, oxygen, and nutrients to cells and transports waste products away from cells?
e: Your circulatory system works like a cheerful delivery highway, pumping blood to drop off oxygen and carry away everyday trash!

q: Which of the following molecules primarily functions to carry electrons from one place to another inside a cell:
e: Think of NAD+ as a tiny, helpful shuttle bus that zips around your cells, picking up and dropping off busy little electrons.

q: Which of the following best describes the position of a gene on a chromosome?
e: Just like your house has a street address, every gene has its own exact neighborhood address called a locus.

q: In humans, olfactory receptors are primarily located in which of the following locations?
e: Up inside your nose, special olfactory receptors wait like eager detectives to sniff out smells from warm cookies to stinky socks.

q: To what group of plants do sequoias belong?
e: Mighty sequoias belong to the conifer family because these gentle forest giants proudly wear cones to protect their seeds!

q: What portion of the human digestive system is responsible for nearly all nutrient absorption?
e: Despite its humble name, your long, winding small intestine is the superstar that absorbs almost every yummy nutrient from your food.

q: In a cell, the presence or absence of a nucleus distinguishes between:
e: Having a cozy nucleus is what separates fancy eukaryotes from simple prokaryotes, who let their DNA swim free and wild!

q: Which of the following is not an ectotherm?
e: Playful otters make their own toasty body heat to stay warm in cold water, so they are not cold-blooded ectotherms.

q: Which of the following interactions is the best example of commensalism?
a: A cleaner fish eats parasites from a larger fish
An oak tree blocks the sunlight of a nearby sapling
A wasp lays its eggs inside of a caterpillar
A dung beetle eats the feces of a buffalo
e: That dung beetle gets a feast while the big buffalo is totally unbothered, making it a perfect example of commensalism.

q: A diver finds an underwater cave filled with bacteria that seem to feed on volcanic sulfur vents. What type of organisms are these?
e: Far from sunlight, these chemotrophs power themselves by feasting on hot volcanic chemicals bubbling up from the earth.

q: What is the name of the bone in the human chin?
e: Your mandible is the mighty lower jawbone that lets you chew, talk, and show off your chin.

q: How many teeth do average human adults have?
e: Once an adult smile is fully grown, it has 32 shining teeth ready to team up and crunch every snack!

q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of inbreeding?
a: Farmers get to choose what organisms to breed
The inbred organism may have genetic disorders due to similar alleles
Unlike hybrids, inbred organisms are not very valuable to people
e: When close relatives have babies, matching hidden hiccups in their genes can easily double up and cause harmful disorders.

q: Which of the following is an intracellular parasite:
e: The sneaky malaria parasite loves to hide right inside red blood cells, making itself a cozy intracellular home.

q: Which of the following BEST describes why all mammalian nucleated non-sex cells have the same chromosomes but appear and function in greatly different ways:
a: different cells lose and acquire different genes as they mature
as cells mature they develop different genes
different genes are turned on and off as cells mature
cells transport pieces of chromosomes called plasmids to control how different cells will function and appear
e: Every cell carries the exact same instruction book, but they cleverly switch on only the pages they need!

q: The leaves on coniferous trees have evolved primarily as an adaption against which of the following conditions?
e: Pine needles wear waxy coats to hold water, helping trees survive thirsty conditions when frozen winter soil blocks drinking.

q: Which of the following animals feeds by standing on its head and kicking food in its mouth?
e: An acrobatic barnacle glues its head down and cheerfully kicks food straight into its mouth with its feathery feet.

q: Ribosomes are made of:
e: Ribosomes are tiny kitchen helpers built from nucleic acids and proteins, working side by side to cook up fresh cell recipes.

q: The Platypus is a mammal.
e: Even though this quirky duck-billed swimmer lays eggs, it feeds its babies milk, making it a true mammal!

q: Which of the following cellular organelles does NOT contain DNA?
e: Ribosomes are busy little protein-making factories, but unlike cell control centers, they carry no DNA of their own.

q: If a population initially exhibits logistic growth, which of the following bests describes the net population growth rate after the population reaches the carrying capacity?
e: When an animal neighborhood runs completely out of room, new births and deaths balance out, making the growth rate zero.

q: The presence of which of the following is the most important characteristic that allows xylem to function in plants:
e: Xylem acts like a mighty drinking straw, using thick, sturdy walls so it does not collapse while slurping water upward!

q: Which of the following terms most commonly refers to nerves leaving the brain:
e: Efferent nerves are like speedy little messengers that exit the brain, happily carrying marching orders to the rest of the body.

q: Which of the following is the male pollen-producing reproductive part of a flower?
e: Like tiny dusted wands, stamens stand tall inside the flower to make golden pollen for visiting bees.

q: When plant scientists began crossing different pure lines, they noticed that the hybrid plants that resulted were:
a: Equally as vigorous as their parents
e: When two different plant families team up, their hybrid seedlings often sprout into stronger, healthier champions than either parent!

q: In which of the following situations would it be most helpful for a patient to take an antihistamine?
a: After getting scratched by a rusty nail
e: Antihistamines calm your body down when allergies make you sneeze and itch over harmless specks of pollen!

q: In mammals, in which of the following is the cochlea located?
e: Tucked deep inside your ear rests the cochlea, a tiny snail-shaped wonder that catches vibrations so you can hear!

q: Which of the following best describes the role of most white blood cells?
e: White blood cells are your body’s loyal little security guards, bravely chasing away sneaky germs to lead your immune response.

q: Which of the following are homologous structures:
a: wing of a bat and the arm of a human
leg of a cat and the wing of a fly
stinger of a bee and the fang of a snake
rattler of a rattle snake and the whistle of a song bird
e: A bat wing and a human arm share the exact same bone blueprint, just cleverly reshaped for soaring or waving.

q: Which of the following is an example of a jawless fish?
e: A lamprey swims through the deep without any jaws, happily using its round suction-cup mouth to find food.

q: Which of the following is a nonvascular plant?
e: Moss hugs damp rocks closely because it lacks the internal plumbing tubes that vascular plants use to carry water.

q: Which of the following is the pH of the normal human stomach lumen?
e: Your stomach is a bubbly little cauldron with strong digestive acid at a pH of 2 to 3 to melt down lunch.

q: Toads and salamanders live in water and on land. They are both examples of:
e: Toads and salamanders are amphibians because they live double lives, splashing as babies in water before exploring the land!

q: Which of the following organisms cannot perform photosynthesis?
e: Mushrooms might sprout in the soil, but they lack green chlorophyll and must absorb decaying snacks instead of cooking with sunshine.

q: For a certain uncatalyzed reaction, a chemist observes that the rate of the reaction appears to double with every 10-kelvin increase in temperature. The chemist then adds a human enzyme that is known to increase the reaction rate one million-fold within its effective temperature and does the same experiment. Which of the following will they likely observe at some stage in the experiement?
a: The reaction rate doubles every 10 kelvin increase in temperature over all temperature ranges
The reaction rate more than doubles every 10 kelvin increase in temperature over all temperature ranges
The reaction rate more than doubles every 10 kelvin increase until a certain temperature, then begins to decrease
The reaction rate less than doubles every 10 kelvin increase in temperature over all temperature ranges
e: The tiny enzyme zooms faster as it warms up, but if things get too hot, it loses its shape and slows down.

q: Which of the following is a rasp-like feeding structure found in many mollusks:
e: Snails and other mollusks scrape up their dinner using a radula, a wondrous tongue covered in tiny, file-like teeth.

q: Given that p equals the frequency of the dominant allele and that q equals the frequency of the recessive allele, which of the following equations does NOT correctly represent a Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
a: p2 + 2pq + q2 = (p + q)2 [p squared plus 2 p q plus q squared equals, open parenthesis, p plus q, close parenthesis, squared]
e: Nature balances genes with squared numbers, so the weird scrambled formula 2p + pq + 2q = 1 does not belong.

q: In which part of the plant would you expect to find the largest concentration of photosynthetic pigments?
e: Leaves are a plant's sun-catching solar panels, packed with green pigments to soak up all the light they can!

q: Which of the following types of diversity is the most difficult to effectively and sustainably improve?
e: Rebuilding a whole ecosystem means balancing countless plants, animals, soil, and weather, making ecosystem diversity the hardest to restore.

q: Which of the following membrane transport methods is most important for release of neurotransmitters like acetylcholine during synaptic signaling?
e: In exocytosis, tiny bubbles fuse with the cell's outer wall to politely deliver chemical messages to their neighbors.

q: In the process of meiosis, which of the following is the end product?
a: One parent cell becomes two daughter cells
One parent cell becomes four daughter cells
Two parent cells become one daughter cell
Two parent cells become two daughter cells
e: Like a magical family tree, one hardworking cell divides twice to welcome four brand-new daughter cells into the world.

q: Which of the following best describes how fungi feed?
a: Some are photoautotrophs, while others are chemoautotrophs
e: Fungi are heterotrophs because they cannot whip up food from sunshine, so they happily absorb tasty nutrients from their surroundings.

q: Which of the following locations primarily consists of smooth muscle?
e: Your stomach is made of smooth muscle, gently churning and mashing your lunch without you ever having to think about it.

q: Which of the following correctly matches an order of amphibians and its characteristics?
a: Squamata: legs, clawed toes and external ears
e: Strange and wonderful Apoda amphibians look like wiggly worms, sporting tiny sensory tentacles and hidden, fishlike scales.

q: If both parents are heterozygous [hetero-ZYE-gus] for a Mendelian [men-DAY-lee-an] trait, what is the percent probability that an offspring is homozygous recessive for that trait?
e: When both parents carry a hidden gene, there is a one-in-four chance, or 25 percent, that their baby gets both!

q: Most of the heart is composed of which of the following types of tissues:
e: Your heart is a mighty engine built mostly of muscle tissue so it can squeeze and pump blood all day long.

q: Which of the following are abiotic factors?
e: Sunlight is an abiotic factor because, unlike plants and animals, the sun's warm rays were never actually alive.

q: Pepper the cat that likes to hunt. He brings home the skull of an unidentified animal with very sharp and robust canines. What did this unknown animal most likely eat?
e: Those pointy teeth were built like tiny steak knives to grip and tear meat, not munch on leafy salads!

q: In which of the following places would meiosis most likely occur in a mammal:
e: Meiosis has the special job of making egg cells, which is why it happens inside the mother's ovary.

q: To control cross-pollination in his experiments, Gregor Mendel removed what pollen-producing organ of the flower?
e: Mendel carefully snipped off the stamens, the flower's pollen makers, so his peas could not pollinate themselves.

q: During which stage of mitosis do the chromosomes line up in the center of the nucleus?
e: In metaphase, chromosomes shuffle like dancers into a neat, straight line right across the middle of the cell.

q: A trans-Pacific flight passenger experiences difficulty adjusting to the difference in time zones. Which of the following supplements may ease the symptoms of jet lag?
e: Melatonin is your body's sleepy bedtime whisper, telling your brain it is finally time to snooze in a new time zone.

q: Which of the following is the BEST reason why high salt environments are difficult environments for organisms to survive in:
a: salt is an ionic molecule and causes a charge differential
salt causes an osmotic imbalance leading to excessive loss of water from cells
salt usually is contaminated with toxic heavy metals
salt causes heavy metal poisons to be readily absorbed through skin
e: Thirsty salt pulls water right out of living cells, leaving them dry and shriveled like a forgotten raisin.

q: In 1986, Lynn Margulis proposed the endosymbiont [en- doh-SIM-be-ont] theory. Which of the following is NOT evidence for this recent theory?
a: Mitochondria [my-tuh-KON-dree-uh] and chloroplasts reproduce by fission
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain their own DNA, which is arranged in a circular pattern as found in prokaryotes [proh-KAR-ee-ohts]
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain peptidoglycan [pep-TI-doh-GLY-kuhn] in their outer membranes like some prokaryotes
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain ribosomes that resemble ribosomes [RY-buh-sohms] in prokaryotes
e: Mitochondria and chloroplasts do not wear peptidoglycan coats on their outer walls, making that the one claim that is not real proof.

q: The human hip is an example of what type of joint?
e: Your hip bone fits snugly like a ball in a cup, making it a ball-and-socket joint that lets you dance!

q: The geologic periods where birds and flowering plants emerged are part of what era?
e: Long ago during the Mesozoic era, while dinosaurs stomped around, the very first birds took flight and colorful flowers blossomed!

q: After a forest fire, annual plants will begin growing in the burnt area fairly quickly. Which of the following best explains why?
a: Forest fires do not usually kill all of the local trees
Forest fires expose bare rock, which is a good substrate for annual plant growth
As a climax community, forests cannot be destroyed
Forest fires do not destroy the topsoil, which supports plant growth
e: Even after a roaring blaze, the rich topsoil stays safe below, holding cozy dirt where fresh seeds can quickly sprout.

q: Which of the following is the region of the body where the stapes bone is located:
e: Tucked deep inside your ear, the tiny stapes bone acts like a miniature stirrup, wiggling to help you hear every sound.

q: Down syndrome is a condition associated with which of the following genetic abnormalities?
e: Down syndrome happens when cells gently pack an extra copy of chromosome 21, making three instead of the usual two.

q: Botanists successfully created viable offspring between two different bamboos that live in the same forest, but noticed that these two species flower during different seasons. Which of the following types of isolation is occurring?
e: Because these bamboos bloom in different seasons, their clocks do not match, creating temporal isolation based purely on time.

q: Immunoglobulins are an example of which of the following?
e: These microscopic defenders, also called antibodies, are specially folded proteins built like tiny grabber tools to catch sneaky germs.

q: Eusociality [yoo-soh-shee-AL-ih-dee] and intraspecies communication are most apparent in which of the following groups of insects?
e: Ants are super team players who build busy underground cities and talk to each other using secret scent trails.

q: Which of the following proteins is the most highly conserved across all living organisms?
e: From tiny bacteria to blue whales, all life shares RNA polymerase to carefully copy our precious recipe books of life.

q: Which of the following is responsible for speeding up the transmission of action potentials across axons?
e: Myelin wraps around nerves like a slippery winter coat, helping brain messages zoom super fast from head to toe!

q: Which of the following molecules is an important part of membrane structure, is usually NOT soluble in water, and stores about 9 kilocalories of energy in each gram?
e: Lipids are clever fats that hate water and build cell walls, packing heaps of energy into every tiny drop.

q: Phosphorus is critical to the formation of nucleic acids, ATP and other energy storing molecules. Where are the largest reservoirs for this important mineral on Earth?
e: Most of Earth's phosphorus is locked deep inside ancient ocean rocks, patiently snoozing under the seafloor for millions of years.

q: In which of the following cells would myelin most likely be found:
e: Myelin wraps around long neurons like a snug winter coat, helping thoughts and signals zoom through your nerves.

q: A summary reaction for photosynthesis is:
a: CO2 + O2 + H2O and light yields carbohydrate + O2
CO2 + H2O and light yields carbohydrate + O2
CO2 + H2O and light yields carbohydrate + H2O
CO2 + O2 + H2O and light yields carbohydrate + H2O
e: Hungry green leaves drink water, breathe carbon dioxide, and catch sunshine to bake sweet sugars while puffing out fresh oxygen!

q: Which of the following choices is an example of a continuous variation?
e: Height is a continuous variation because we do not come in set sizes, but grow along a smooth, sliding scale.

q: Which of the following is the MOST common manner for transmission of beef tapeworms to humans:
e: Eating uncooked beef can let hidden tapeworm travelers sneak into a tummy, so cooking meat keeps everyone safe.

q: What causes Lyme disease?
e: Sneaky corkscrew-shaped bacteria hitch a ride on tiny ticks, sneaking inside their host to cause Lyme disease.

q: Which of the following is NOT found in both bacterial and human cells?
e: Our cells pack their precious DNA inside a neat little control center called a nucleus, but free-spirited bacteria let theirs wander loose!

q: The conversion of glucose to carbon dioxide and water is an example of what type of reaction?
e: Breaking down big glucose molecules into carbon dioxide and water releases energy, making it a catabolic reaction.

q: A new vertebrate organism is discovered. It reproduces by laying an amniotic [am-nee-AWT-ik] egg. It also produces milk. Which of the following terms best classifies this animal?
e: Monotremes are wonderful oddballs like the platypus, laying leathery eggs yet still nursing their babies with milk.

q: Pasteur advanced the understanding of disease through which of the following?
a: Collecting data indicating that viruses can cause disease
Collecting data indicating that bacteria can cause disease
Providing a method to identify pathogens
e: Louis Pasteur gathered clever clues showing that tiny, invisible bacteria are the sneaky troublemakers causing disease.

q: The breakdown of molecules to obtain energy is which of the following?
e: Catabolism acts like a friendly wrecking crew, breaking down big food molecules to release bursts of energy your body can use.

q: Which of the following functional groups is possessed by alcohols?
e: Every alcohol molecule proudly wears a hydroxyl group, where an oxygen and a hydrogen atom hold hands like best friends.

q: Which of the following is the difference between a viroid [VY-roid] and a virus?
a: Viroids do not contain a protein coat; viruses do
Viroids only contain RNA; viruses also contain protein
Viroids only contain DNA; viruses also contain protein
Viroids contain DNA; viruses do not
e: Viruses bundle up in cozy protein coats, but viroids bravely venture out bare, skipping that protective outer jacket entirely.

q: Agar is derived from what organism?
e: Red algae sway beneath ocean waves, making a squishy gel called agar that scientists borrow to grow microscopic little friends.

q: In bean and corn seeds, the food supply that is used by the seed to germinate and grow is in the:
e: Think of the cotyledon as a baby sprout's packed lunchbox, full of yummy snacks until it can make its own food!

q: Which of the following processes is MOST under the influence of the hormone aldosterone?
e: Aldosterone works like a tiny referee inside you, balancing sodium and potassium salts so your body stays happily hydrated.

q: Which of the following adjectives best describes the spores that are produced during fungal asexual reproduction?
e: These fungal spores travel light as haploid explorers, carrying just one single set of genetic instructions from their parent.

q: What gland, located in the area beneath the sternum, is essential for a fully functional immune system?
e: Snuggled behind your breastbone, the thymus acts like a cozy school where your body's brave defender cells train to fight germs.

q: Which of the following terms best describes groups of rabbits, foxes, deer, and birds living in a temperate deciduous forest?
e: When different critters like foxes and deer share a forest neighborhood, they form a lively community living side by side.

q: In which of the following organs would one find the greatest amount of keratin proteins?
e: Your skin packs in tons of tough keratin protein, weaving a water-resistant shield to protect your whole body.

q: Neuraminidase [NOOR-ah-MIN-ih-dase] is present on the surface of the influenza virus. Which of the following statements best describes the mechanism through which neuraminidase inhibitors, or NAIs, act to limit viral spread?
a: NAIs inhibit integration of the viral genome into the host genome
NAIs limit replication by preventing the release of virions [VEER-ee-ons] from the infected cell
NAIs directly bind viral RNA sequences to prevent reverse transcription
NAIs are incorporated into host ribosome complexes and limit translation of viral proteins
e: These medicine helpers lock the cell door, trapping newly formed flu particles inside so they cannot spread.

q: Often, an enzyme requires the presence of another small molecule in order to function. What is the term for these small molecules?
e: Enzymes are superstar workers, but they need trusty sidekick molecules called cofactors to help them do their jobs!

q: Aggregation of tau protein and formation of beta-amyloid plaques are hallmarks of which of the following human diseases?
e: In Alzheimer's, sticky plaques and tangled proteins clutter up brain pathways like dusty cobwebs, confusing precious memories.

q: Which of the following statements does NOT support the cell theory?
a: All organisms are composed of cells
Cells are the fundamental units of living organisms
e: Cells cannot just poof out of thin air! Every tiny cell alive today came from another cell that lived before it.

q: In ecology, what does the term detritus refer to?
e: Detritus is nature's fallen feast of dead leaves and decaying bits, waiting for hungry soil critters to recycle it.

q: Which of the following junctions forms a water-tight seal?
e: Adherent junctions act like waterproof glue, zipping cells tightly together so not a single drop leaks past.

q: Plasmids that are used in laboratory methods typically originate from which of the following groups of organisms?
e: Plasmids naturally come from bacteria, who carry these tiny bonus rings of DNA like secret trading cards.

q: Which of the following is NOT a distinguishing characteristic of members of the subphylum Crustacea?
a: Walking legs present on the abdomen
e: Crustaceans wear their walking legs along their chest, so having walking legs on the abdomen is definitely not a crustacean trait.

q: The "Gympie Stinger" is the deadliest plant in the world.
e: That prickly bush packs a fiercely painful sting, but other sneaky plants hold much deadlier poisons.

q: Mollusks possess a flexible, tongue-shaped feeding structure called what?
e: Meet the radula, a snail's scratchy little tongue that scrapes up tasty snacks like a tiny cheese grater!

q: Your knees are an example of which of the following types of joint?
e: Just like a squeaky door opening and closing in one direction, your knee bends back and forth like a sturdy hinge joint.

q: A sea dragon mimics what to stay camouflaged?
e: Floating gently through the waves, a clever sea dragon grows leafy parts to look just like seaweed and trick hungry neighbors.

q: Which of the following organisms has the most recent common ancestor with humans?
e: On the giant family tree of life, chimpanzees sit on the branch right next to us as our closest cousins.

q: Lecithin is an example of which of the following?
e: Lecithin is a busy little phospholipid, a special kind of fat that helps bubbly water and oil play nicely together.

q: Which of the following organisms is probably the most commonly studied prokaryote?
e: Meet E. coli, the most famous bacterium on Earth! Curious scientists have studied this little swimmer more than any other prokaryote.

q: In the human body, the gallbladder is in immediate proximity to what organ?
e: Your little gallbladder snuggles right beneath the big liver, gladly catching and storing its digestive juices.

q: Which of the following is NOT a gymnosperm?
e: While gymnosperms proudly build cones with seeds, simple little hornworts are ancient plants that make tiny spores instead.

q: Estuaries, like wetlands, are extremely productive in terms of biotic factors. What is the main source of the nutrients that facilitate the metabolic processes necessary for this productivity?
e: A rushing river acts like a delivery truck, carrying rich dirt and tasty plant food straight down to the busy estuary.

q: What is the scientific name for the "Polar Bear"?
e: Scientists call the polar bear Ursus maritimus, meaning sea bear, because this snowy giant loves paddling through icy waters.

q: Which of the following is most accurate about the pasteurization of milk:
a: it kills all bacteria by sterilizing the milk
it reduces the population of bacteria by heating but not boiling the milk
e: Pasteurization gently warms milk just enough to defeat harmful bacteria without boiling away all the creamy goodness.

q: Experiments crossing different colored pea plants demonstrate what genetic concept?
e: Those colorful peas showed how bold dominant traits can hide quiet recessive traits until they pop up in baby plants.

q: An organism's way of life, including its habitat, food, predators, and other organisms it competes with for resources make up an organism's:
e: An animal's special job, home, and daily routine fit together like a puzzle piece called its ecological niche.

q: Which of the following is true of osmosis?
a: Osmosis is the movement of water from a region of high solute concentration to a region of low solute concentration
Osmosis is a form of passive transport
Osmosis cannot occur across a semi-permeable membrane
Osmosis involves the active transport of solute and requires ATP
e: Osmosis is passive transport because water flows across barriers all on its own, without the cell spending any energy.

q: A scientist discovers a new single-cell organism that can concurrently produce mRNA from DNA and read the mRNA to produce protein. What is the likeliest classification of this organism?
e: Without a walled-off room for their DNA, speedy bacteria can read instructions and build proteins at the exact same time.

q: The antibiotic penicillin halts bacterial growth by doing which of the following?
a: Interfering with the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall
Interfering with the synthesis of bacterial ribosomes
Preventing attachment of messenger RNA to the ribosome
e: Penicillin stops sneaky bacteria from building their tough outer cell walls, leaving them defenseless and unable to grow.

q: Which of the following is an example of a carbohydrate?
e: Glucose is a sweet simple sugar, making it the classic carbohydrate fuel that powers everything from playground tag to daydreaming.

q: Glucose, sucrose, fructose, and lactose are all examples of which of the following?
e: These sweet names are all carbohydrates, sugary little fuel packs that give your body quick energy to run and play!

q: You are playing outside when the neighbor's child comes running up to you screaming that he's been bitten by a snake. You look at the small wound, and immediately notice a very foul smell on his hands. Which of the following snakes most likely bit him?
e: When startled, a harmless garter snake defends itself by releasing a super stinky goo that leaves quite a smelly clue.

q: Which of the following geologic periods was ended by a major mass extinction?
e: The Cretaceous period went out with a bang when a giant space rock wiped out the mighty dinosaurs.

q: Which of the following terms is used to describe a change in cell structure and function from generalized to specialized?
e: Through differentiation, a plain little cell discovers its true passion and transforms into a superstar heart or brain cell.

q: Which of the following is the most practical method that could be used to isolate proteins for reinjection into mice?
e: Affinity chromatography gently catches the exact proteins you want, keeping them healthy and ready to help a mouse.

q: Which of the following is the scientific name for the part of the human brain where higher brain operations occur such as thinking, imagination, mathematical reasoning and language:
e: Your wrinkly cerebral cortex is the master control room where your deepest thoughts, bright daydreams, and clever ideas come alive.

q: Which of the following is the correct botanical term for the stem of a flower:
e: A peduncle is the strong green stalk that proudly lifts a flower up to greet the warm sun.

q: Which of the following molecules is most commonly used for the transport of energy in cells?
e: Think of ATP as a rechargeable battery, zooming around inside cells to deliver power everywhere it is needed!

q: A new organism is discovered. Dissection of the creature reveals a digestive tract, segmented body, no vertebrae , and only bilateral symmetry. What phylum [FYE-lum] should it be categorized under?
e: With neatly segmented rings and a cozy gut inside, this squirmy invertebrate fits right into the earthworm family called Annelida.

q: Which of the following portions of the nervous system controls involuntary responses during times of stress?
e: When danger pops up, your sympathetic nervous system swoops in, making your heart race so you can zoom away!

q: Which of the following does NOT occur in mitosis:
e: Chromosomes dance solo in mitosis, saving their special partner hug called synapsis only for meiosis.

q: Suppose your biological mother has blood type A and your biological father has blood type AB. Which of the following is definitely NOT your blood type?
e: Dad has genes for A and B, so he always passes one along, meaning a baby can never end up with type O!

q: Which of the following is the principle difference between the two types of active transport?
a: Primary active transport involves an electrochemical gradient, while secondary active transport involves chemical energy
Primary active transport involves chemical energy, while secondary active transport involves an electrochemical gradient
Primary active transport involves moving ions into a cell, while secondary active transport involves moving ions out of a cell
Primary active transport involves moving ions out of a cell, while secondary active transport involves moving ions into a cell
e: Primary transport burns chemical fuel directly, while secondary transport smartly hitches a ride on an electric slope of charged particles.

q: Which of the following is the primary feeding pattern for Cnidarians [ny-DAIR-ee-uhns]?
e: With stinging tentacles waiting like tiny fishing poles, cnidarians are sneaky carnivores that love snacking on passing meat.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the innate immune system?
e: While innate guards rush in instantly, clever antibodies take time to study the enemy and remember them later.

q: Plant metabolism must:
a: Produce carbon dioxide and consume oxygen
Neither produce nor consume carbon dioxide or oxygen
Consume carbon dioxide and produce oxygen
Both produce and consume carbon dioxide and oxygen
e: Plants make and use both oxygen and carbon dioxide, balancing making food in sunshine with breathing day and night.

q: Proteins can be separated by which of the following?
e: Chromatography lets proteins race through a special obstacle course, neatly sorting them as different ones finish at different speeds.

q: Which of the following contributes to the hydrophobicity of lipids?
a: Water is polar and lipids are non-polar
Water and lipids are both polar
Water and lipids are both non-polar
Water is non-polar and lipids are polar
e: Water molecules love clinging to each other because they are polar, leaving non-polar lipids locked out of the party.

q: Which of the following statements best describes the primary difference between animal centrosomes and plant centrosomes?
a: Plant centrosomes have a rough exterior made of cellulose
Plant centrosomes do not have centrioles
Animal centrosomes are in the cytoplasm
e: While animal centrosomes use tiny barrel-shaped helpers called centrioles, plant centrosomes cleverly organize cell division completely without them.

q: Which of the following is a genetic disorder caused by aneuploidy [an-yoo-PLOI-dee]?
e: Down syndrome happens when cells accidentally pack an extra chromosome into the suitcase, a mix-up known as aneuploidy.

q: What is the national bird of Bahrain?
e: With its sweet singing voice and friendly charm, the lovely bulbul proudly serves as Bahrain's beloved national bird.

q: Which of the following organisms is considered to be a crustacean?
e: A copepod is a tiny, paddle-footed crustacean swimming through the sea like an adorable underwater flea!

q: Which of the following BEST describes the chemical makeup of a human chromosome:
e: A chromosome is the ultimate buddy team, sharing space almost equally between precious DNA recipes and cozy protein helpers.

q: Which of the following is an example of a monotreme (read as: MOH-noh-treem)?
e: The delightful platypus is a monotreme because this quirky mammal surprises the world by laying eggs instead of giving birth to live babies.

q: Which of these species is not extinct?
e: While the others have vanished into history, mighty Komodo dragons are still happily stomping around their sunny island homes today!

q: Which of the following is NOT an accurate comparison between meiosis [my-OH-sis] and mitosis [my-TOH-sis]?
a: During metaphase in mitosis, chromosomes line up at the equator, while during metaphase I, homologous [huh-MOL-uh-guhs] pairs line up at the equator
In prophase in mitosis, chromosomes are made of two sister chromatids [KROH-muh-tids], while in prophase I, homologous chromosomes form tetrads
In both anaphase in mitosis and anaphase I of meiosis, sister chromatids separate
Mitosis produces two identical cells, while meiosis produces four daughter cells
e: During anaphase one, sister chromatids hold hands and stay together while pairs split, so they do not separate in both!

q: What is the primary purpose of floral nectar?
a: It is produced as a food source for the plant
It is produced as a byproduct of plant metabolism
It reduces the randomness of pollination
It is used as an antibiotic to protect the plant from microbes
e: Sweet nectar is a flower's tasty bribe, inviting busy animal helpers to visit directly so spreading pollen is never left to random chance.

q: If a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution, what effect will osmosis have on the cell?
a: It will become turgid or lyse
e: Water rushes inside like a filling balloon, making the plant cell puff up tight or even burst open!

q: Tigers have one colour of skin despite the stripey fur.
e: That is false! A tiger's famous stripes are actually printed right on its skin, hidden underneath that fuzzy coat.

q: What is the name for a male bee that comes from an unfertilized egg?
e: Meet the drone, a gentle boy bee born without a father who spends his sunny days relaxing around the busy hive.

q: Which of the following techniques is best used to diagnose a disease caused by aneuploidy (read as: AHN-yuh-plohi-dee)?
e: Karyotyping lines up all of a cell's chromosomes for a neat family photo, helping scientists count them to spot any extra or missing ones.

q: Respiration is part of the biogeochemical cycle for which of the following elements?
e: Every time living things breathe out, they send carbon dioxide puffing into the air, keeping carbon traveling on its grand circle through nature.

q: Which of the following types of organisms caused the potato famine in Ireland in the 1800s?
e: A sneaky, plant-munching protist invaded Ireland's potato fields, destroying crops because this tiny organism spread faster than anyone could stop it.

q: Which of the following structures can be found in an E. coli cell?
e: Tiny E. coli skips the fancy compartments, but it keeps busy little ribosomes around to build essential proteins!

q: Assume a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution. Which of the following will happen to the cell?
a: The pressure inside the cell will increase
The pressure inside the cell will remain the same
The pressure inside the cell will decrease
Dissolved particles outside the cell will move into the cell
e: Water eagerly rushes inside the cell like an overfilled balloon, pushing against the walls and making the pressure inside rise!

q: You have discovered a new bacterium. You notice that this bacterium can use light to create ATP, but is reliant on other prokaryotes [proh-KAR-ee-ohts] to obtain organic carbon. The bacterium is most likely which of the following?
e: This clever bacterium catches sunlight for energy but snacks on neighbors for carbon, which makes it a sun-powered photoheterotroph.

q: The similarities between the lungs of a reptile and the air bladder of a fish can be described, in evolutionary terms, as:
e: They are homologous structures because reptiles and fish inherited this shared organ design from an ancient ancestor, like a cherished family heirloom.

q: Plastids surrounded by a double membrane are evidence for what?
e: Like packing a lunch inside a lunchbox, secondary endosymbiosis happened when one cell swallowed another, wrapping it in two cozy protective blankets.

q: Huge groups of which of the following migrating animals stop traffic on Australia's Christmas Island every year?
e: Millions of bright red crabs march across roads toward the ocean, creating a crawling red carpet that brings island traffic to a halt!

q: Which of the following is a theory of heredity postulated by Lamarck:
a: characteristics acquired after birth are passed on to following generations
nature selects for the best characteristic
only the fittest organisms survive through natural selection
e: Lamarck believed that traits you gain during your own life, like stretched muscles, get passed right down to your children.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered connective tissue?
e: Connective tissues act like glue holding parts together, but muscles do their own bouncy work of squeezing and pulling!

q: In which of the following stages in the life of an average dividing cell would it spend most of its time:
e: Cells spend most of their busy days in interphase, growing big and copying recipes before splitting into two!

q: Which of the following correctly explains why glucose is converted to glucose-6-phosphate in the first step of glycolysis [glye-KAWL-eh-sis]?
a: The cell membrane is impermeable to large, negatively-charged molecules
It enables the splitting of glucose in half during the next step
The isomerization [eye-saw-mor-eyes-AY-shun] of glucose is less favorable than that of glucose-6-phosphate
Glucose-6-phosphate can also be incorporated into glycogen [GLYE-koh-jen]
e: Adding a charged tag traps glucose inside, because the cell membrane will not let large, negative molecules slip away.

q: When water accidentally enters your trachea, sensory neurons send information through a reflex arc in the brain to trigger coughing. In what structure in the nervous system are the interneurons of this reflex arc located?
e: Meet your medulla, the trusty brain stem helper that instantly triggers a big cough whenever water tickles the wrong pipe.

q: Which of the following is NOT a structure found in human cells:
e: Plants wear stiff cell walls like crunchy armor, but our squishy human cells happily skip them to stay flexible.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the primary function of a protein enzyme:
a: a catalyst made of amino acids
a string of amino acids added to a sugar to make the sugar stronger
as a short term form of energy storage
e: Built from amino acids, an enzyme acts like a speedy helper called a catalyst, zipping up chemical reactions inside your body.

q: Which of the following is a general term widely used by scientists to indicate artificial growth of cells in the laboratory:
e: When scientists give tiny cells a cozy dish and warm broth to multiply in a lab, they call it a culture!

q: Which of the following organs is NOT part of the endocrine system?
e: While endocrine glands send hormone messages, your hard-working spleen focuses on filtering blood and fighting germs instead.

q: Which of the following types of carbohydrate is found in animals and is considered to be structural?
e: Chitin is the sturdy sugar building block that gives crabs and beetles their shiny, protective outer suits of armor.

q: Which of the following issues do humans have the most control over when contemplating the release of transgenic animals into the wild?
a: Competition between transgenic and wild populations
Movement of the altered gene into the wild gene pool
Different niche requirements with the transgenic versus wild populations
e: Scientists can directly choose whether genetically changed fish are able to survive or reproduce before ever letting them swim free.

q: What color/colour is a polar bear's skin?
e: Under all that fluffy white fur, a polar bear actually has black skin to soak up every drop of sunshine!

q: A bacterium is suddenly immersed in a high salt media. What is the MOST likely response of the cell?
a: Actively transport water into the cell
Actively transport water out of the cell
Actively transport potassium into the cell
Actively transport small organic molecules out of the cell
e: Surrounded by salty water, the tiny bacterium rushes potassium inside itself to keep its own moisture from escaping.

q: A pair of gene homologs are from a mouse and a human, respectively. Which of the following gene regions is likely to be most well-conserved?
e: Exons hold the precious recipes for building working proteins, so nature keeps them carefully protected across humans and mice.

q: Which of the following is the most likely effect on the remaining bacteria after killing 90% of bacteria with antibacterial soap?
a: They will reproduce and form a colony of bacteria that are more resistant
They will die because there are not enough bacteria left to reproduce
They can no longer cause infections because their numbers are too low
e: The few tough germ survivors throw a victory party, multiplying into a brand-new super squad that can resist your soap!

q: Though T-cells originate in bone marrow, where in the human body do they mature?
e: Tiny T-cells travel to the thymus, a cozy little school where they grow into mighty germ-fighting defenders.

q: Which of the following anatomical adjectives is NOT correctly described?
e: Rostral actually means near the nose or beak, like a bird's snout, not back by the wagging tail!

q: Which of the following groups of viruses needs to be in the nucleus of a eukaryotic host to replicate, as opposed to the cytoplasm?
e: Clever herpesviruses sneak past the outer cell goo and unpack their genetic copies right inside the cozy cell nucleus.

q: Which of the following hormones most directly affects the metabolic rate of the body?
e: Triiodothyronine acts like your body's personal gas pedal, directly telling cells how fast to burn fuel and make energy.

q: Which of these is a stop codon in DNA?
e: Just like a tiny red traffic light, the DNA letters TAA tell your body to stop building a protein!

q: Which of the following is true regarding the major difference between cellulose and glycogen [GLY-kuh-juhn]?
a: Cellulose is a polymer of galactose [guh-LAK-thos], while glycogen is a polymer of glucose
Cellulose is mostly found in animal cells, while glycogen is mostly found in plant cells
Cellulose consists of beta glycosidic [gly-kuh-SY-dik] linkages, while glycogen consists of alpha glycosidic linkages
Cellulose is highly branched, while glycogen is linear
e: Cellulose builds stiff plant walls using flat beta bonds, while friendly glycogen stores energy with bendy alpha bonds.

q: In early experiments in the mid-1900's, the source and fate of oxygen involved in photosynthesis was mostly determined through experiments that used:
a: animals in closed containers that would die unless a plant was introduced into the container
a heavy isotope of oxygen as a tracer
fluorescent labeling of various enzymes and organic products
simple accounting of the atomic mass of all the reactants and products
e: Clever scientists tagged oxygen atoms with heavy isotopes, tracking them like little glowing backpacks through the plant's sunny recipe.

q: Where is the most likely place to find an animal that is an osmoconformer [oz-moh-kuhn-FOHR-mer]?
e: Ocean critters happily match the saltiness of the sea around them, making marine waters the perfect home for osmoconformers.

q: Which of the following cell types is associated with haversian [ha-VER-zhen] canals?
e: Cozy osteocyte bone cells live inside tiny tunnel highways called Haversian canals, sharing snacks like friendly underground neighbors.

q: Beadle and Tatum's one gene-one enzyme hypothesis was formed from the results of their investigation of which of the following biological processes?
e: Mold cooks up its own tiny protein blocks! Scientists saw that broken genes stopped mold from making amino acids, proving genes control those recipes.

q: Which of the following best describes actin treadmilling?
a: New actin polymers attach to the minus end of the actin filament
The actin filament remains static with no addition or loss of subunits
One end of an actin filament has a net addition of actin polymers while the other end has a net loss of actin polymers
One end of the actin filament adds and loses polymers at an equal rate
e: Picture a conveyor belt building itself! Tiny actin pieces click onto one busy end while tumbling right off the other, keeping it moving in place.

q: Ducklings learn to recognize and follow the first moving object that they see, usually their mother. What is this behavior called?
e: A newborn duckling opens its eyes and immediately follows the first friend it sees. This quick bonding superpower is called imprinting!

q: Which of the following marine fish groups reproduces ovoviviparously [oh-voh-vy-vip-ER-uhs-lee]?
e: Deep down in the ocean, mother coelacanths keep their eggs safe inside until they hatch, giving birth to live, swimming babies!

q: All of the following factors increase the release of oxygen from hemoglobin in systemic capillaries, EXCEPT:
e: Hemoglobin hugs oxygen tighter when it gets chilly, so a low temperature keeps oxygen bundled up instead of letting it go!

q: Someone has carelessly tossed several sets of human vertebrae into a single box. You are trying to sort out the mess and have counted 20 lumbar, 48 thoracic, and 26 cervical vertebrae. It's now clear you are missing some bones. How many bones are you missing, and what type of vertebrae are they?
e: Four bodies need seven neck bones each, totaling twenty-eight cervical bones. Since you only have twenty-six, two cervical bones are missing!

q: Flowers are actually miniature stems that produce four kinds of specialized:
e: Nature loves to play dress-up! A flower's bright petals and snug parts are really just ordinary leaves wearing colorful party costumes.

q: An inability of body cells to receive adequate amounts of oxygen may indicate a malfunction of:
e: Erythrocytes are like tiny red delivery trucks carrying oxygen throughout your body. If cells are gasping, those little trucks are having car trouble!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about purple-striped jellies?
a: Humans exposed to their nematocysts typically have a fatal reaction
Young cancer crabs are often found clinging to the jelly
They move short distances by pulsing
e: A purple-striped jelly has a painful sting, but it will not kill a human. It is just an ouchie, not a deadly monster!

q: Which of the following codons could NOT result in a nonsense mutation following a single-nucleotide substitution?
e: Stop signals are UAA, UAG, and UGA. Swapping just one letter in AGG can never spell any of those three stop words!

q: If the average fur thickness of wild foxes in the northern hemisphere increased with increasing latitude, this variation would be an example of which of the following.
e: Nature nudges fox coats to grow thicker and thicker as it gets colder, steering the whole population toward one extreme through directional selection!

q: Which of the following mutations would most likely result in a frame-shift mutation?
e: Deleting a single base pulls out one letter, scrambling every three-letter word down the line like a shifted train car!

q: Which of the following hormones is a steroid hormone?
e: Cortisol is crafted from oily cholesterol, making it a true steroid messenger that can slip right through cell walls with ease.

q: Which of the following brain regions is primarily responsible for coordinating basic reflexes like swallowing and vomiting?
e: Deep at your brain's base, the trusty medulla oblongata acts like autopilot, taking charge whenever you need to swallow or suddenly throw up!

q: Which of the following immune cells is most involved in defense against parasites?
e: When pesky parasites try to crash the party, fearless eosinophils rush in, spraying special chemical tools to send those big invaders packing!

q: Which of the following best describes the trophic [TROH-fik] status of a green and highly- productive lake?
e: Packed with yummy nutrients, a eutrophic lake bursts with so much green algae that it looks like a thick, bubbling pea soup!

q: Most angiosperm [AN-jee-oh-sperms] species can be classified in which of the following clades?
e: Flowering plants love showing off, and the biggest family group of all is the eudicots, claiming most of the flowering beauties on Earth!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of globular proteins in mammals:
a: some serve as transport molecules in the plasma
plasma enzymes typically have an optimal operating pH of about 6.8 to 7.0
e: Blood stays nicely balanced at a pH of about 7.4, so its proteins work best there instead of dipping lower into acidic territory.

q: Amniotes became very well adapted to life on land. Which of the following is not an adaptation of amniotes to a terrestrial existence?
e: Frogs gulp air using their cheeks by buccal pumping, but true land amniotes upgraded to breathing deeply with their trusty ribcages instead!

q: Which of the following forms of selection is most conducive for sympatric speciation?
e: Disruptive selection splits a crowd in two by favoring both extremes, helping neighbors in the very same home drift into brand-new species!

q: There are three checkpoints during normal cell division. In what stages in the life of a cell are these checkpoints found?
a: Growth phase I, Growth Phase II, and mitosis
Growth phase I, S phase, and mitosis
S phase, growth phase II, and mitosis
e: A careful cell hits the brakes to check its work during Growth Phase One, Growth Phase Two, and mitosis!

q: Which of the following chromatographic methods is likely to be the most effective for isolating large protein aggregates from smaller protein complexes?
e: In gel filtration chromatography, giant proteins easily roll past tiny sponge holes while smaller ones get trapped.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of chordates?
e: Chordates have matching left and right sides, so circular radial symmetry simply does not fit their shape.

q: What is the name of the largest family of human cell surface receptors that is characterized by a 7-transmembrane domain motif?
e: G-protein coupled receptors are the cell's biggest communication team, weaving across the cell surface seven times to catch secret messages.

q: Compared to a seawater acclimated fish, a freshwater acclimated fish would be expected to have which of the following?
e: Freshwater fish constantly soak up water, so their kidneys use higher filtration rates to pump the extra flood out.

q: With which of the following does human interstitial fluid differ in concentration the most when compared with plasma:
e: Blood vessels keep bulky proteins trapped inside the plasma, leaving very few behind in the fluid between cells.

q: Which of the following is the term for the transfer of genes by viruses from one prokaryote to another:
e: Transduction happens when a sneaky virus acts like a delivery truck, carrying bacterial genes over to a brand-new cell.

q: The terms frustule [fruh-stool], epitheca [epi-thek-uh], and silica apply to which of the following organisms?
e: Diatoms are tiny ocean artists that build sparkling glass houses out of silica, complete with matching top and bottom shells!

q: Which of the following is true regarding the phylum Cnidaria [nihd-air-ee-uh]?
a: Cnidarians include organisms such as flatworms and tapeworms
Cnidarians usually have a motile medusa form and a non-motile polyp form
Cnidarians form three germ layers during development, one of which forms the coelem
Gastropoda is a class within the phylum Cnidaria
e: Cnidarians live two lives: one as a grounded polyp standing tall, and another as a free-swimming medusa dancing in the waves.

q: Which of the following combinations of nutrients results in the greatest increase of ocean primary production?
e: Tiny ocean algae bloom like crazy when they feast on nitrogen, phosphorus, and iron, their ultimate trio of plant food!

q: Lysosomes [LY-suh-sohms] are membrane-enclosed organelles in a cell containing an array of enzymes. Which of the following is closest to the pH of these vesicles?
e: Lysosomes act like bubbling little stomachs inside the cell, staying acidic at a pH around five to digest leftovers.

q: Stomata will open in response to internal and external cues. Which of the following is NOT one of these cues?
a: Decrease of carbon dioxide in leaf air spaces due to photosynthesis in the mesophyll
Mesophyll production of abscisic acid in response to water deficiency
e: When a plant gets thirsty, abscisic acid acts like an emergency brake that slams stomata shut instead of opening them!

q: Metallothionein [meh-talloh-THIGH-uh-nin] is a protein that has been engineered into rice in order to promote iron uptake in the small intestine. This is because iron uptake requires which of the following elements?
e: This helpful protein uses sulfur like sticky glue to grab hold of iron and carry it through the tummy.

q: Leghemoglobin [leg-HEE-muh-gloh-bin] functions as an oxygen binding protein in which of the following?
e: Leghemoglobin cuddles up with oxygen inside plant roots, keeping friendly soil bacteria happy and safe.

q: Membrane depolarization of an action potential is able to pass from one cardiac cell to another through what type of connection between cells?
e: Gap junctions act like open secret doorways between heart cells, letting electrical beats flash through so they pump as one!

q: Which of the following mutations would most likely affect a gene the LEAST:
e: A single base substitution swaps just one letter, leaving the rest of the genetic recipe mostly untouched.

q: Wolves are introduced to an island populated with white-tailed deer. After several generations, the average sprint speed of the deer increased significantly relative to the wolf introduction period. In evolutionary terms, of which of the following kinds of selection is this is an example?
e: Directional selection pushes the whole herd toward one winning trait, helping faster deer survive until speedy runners become the new normal.

q: Which of the following diseases is caused by an apicomplexan [appee-com-PLEX-en]?
e: Malaria is caused by a tiny apicomplexan parasite that hitches a ride inside mosquitoes to sneak into our blood.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a stone fruit?
e: An apple protects its seeds in a papery core rather than one hard, woody stone in the middle.

q: The cotyledon [kot-uhl-EED-uhn] is which of the following?
e: A cotyledon is a baby plant's very first leaf, safely tucked inside the seed until it sprouts into the sunshine!

q: In humans, which of the following blood types would be expected to occur with the highest frequency among the offspring of parents who are both type AB?
e: Each parent passes down an A or a B, so babies have the best fifty-fifty shot of landing on AB.

q: Which of the following statements best describes the thermodynamic effect of an enzyme on the reaction it catalyzes?
a: The energy level of the reactants is decreased in the presence of the enzyme
The activation energy of the reaction is decreased
The activation energy of the reaction is increased
The G [delta-G] between products and reactants is decreased
e: An enzyme is like a friendly helper that lowers a steep hill, decreasing the activation energy needed to start.

q: In embryonic development, the archenteron is a precursor to what?
e: Early in an embryo's story, a tiny folded pocket called the archenteron grows up to become the gut!

q: Which of the following will most likely result from a single base deletion in DNA:
e: Plucking out just one letter shifts the whole reading frame down, scrambling every single word in a frameshift mutation!

q: Which of the following does albumin [al-BYOO-muhn] help to regulate?
e: Albumin acts like a helpful sponge in your bloodstream, soaking up water to balance osmotic pressure.

q: Which of the following molecules would have the most peptide bonds:
e: Hemoglobin is a giant protein made of hundreds of amino acids, all stitched together with tons of peptide bonds.

q: Which of the following eye adaptations allows birds of prey like raptors to maintain high visual sensitivity when diving for prey?
a: Presence of a tapetum lucidum [tuh-PEE-tuhm loo-SEE-duhm]
Ability to change relative amounts of cis and trans retinal
e: With two sharp focus spots called foveas on each eye, diving raptors zoom in on prey like magic!

q: In eukaryotic cells, the electron transport chain directly performs which of the following actions?
a: Pumping protons into the mitochondrial matrix
Pumping protons into the intermembrane space
e: Like busy little pumps, the electron transport chain shovels protons right across into the intermembrane space.

q: The Edinger-Westphal nucleus consists of parasympathetic neurons that control pupillary reflexes. Which of the following neurotransmitters do Edinger-Westphal neurons most likely release?
e: These calm parasympathetic nerves use acetylcholine to whisper instructions to your eyes, telling the pupils to shrink.

q: p53 is a protein associated with which of the following processes?
e: Meet p53, the watchful hall monitor of the cell cycle who halts division if DNA gets hurt!

q: Which of the following provides the best example of a situation in which genetic drift would play a significant role within a population?
a: Non-random mating among plants with purple flowers leads to inbreeding and homozygous lethal conditions that prevent seed germination
In a large population of plants with purple flowers, one individual exhibits white flowers caused by a mutation
In a small population of plants with purple flowers, three white-flowered individuals exist. A deer eats two of the three white flowered plants, thus removing them from the population
In a small population of plants where some individuals have white and some have purple flowers, bees strongly prefer the purple flowers, thus more seeds are produced from the purple individuals.
e: When a deer randomly munches two rare white flowers in a small meadow, genetic drift changes the family forever.

q: An animal's respiratory tidal volume is 500 milliliters and its cardiac output is 250 milliliters per minute with a stroke volume of 5 milliliters. Which of the following is its heart rate in beats per minute?
e: Pumping two hundred fifty milliliters a minute at five milliliters per beat means the heart ticks fifty times.

q: In the Griffith experiment, nonpathogenic bacteria were found to be able to cause disease after being exposed to heat-killed virulent bacteria. Which of the following substances caused this transformation?
e: Even after bad germs were gone, their leftover DNA slipped into harmless neighbors, teaching them how to be wicked.

q: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of the order Hemiptera?
a: Wings that are held "roof-like" over the body when the insect is at rest
Chewing mouthparts that arise from the posterior of the head
Sucking mouthparts that arise from the anterior of the head
e: True bugs carry their very own straw, showing off sucking mouthparts that sprout from the front of their head!

q: Brine shrimp are able to survive in wide ranges of salinity. Which of the following phrases is NOT true regarding their osmoregulation when placed in a tank of saline?
a: Osmoconformation, body fluid osmolarity is equivalent to osmolarity of saline in which they are swimming
Osmoregulation, body fluid osmolarity is kept at an osmolarity different from the osmolarity of saline in which they are swimming
Hyper-osmoregulation, body fluid osmolarity is kept higher than osmolarity of saline in which they are swimming
Hypo-osmoregulation, body fluid osmolarity is kept lower than osmolarity of saline in which they are swimming
e: Brine shrimp never hold more salt inside than the sea, so hyper-osmoregulation is impossible for these salty swimmers.

q: Which of the following is necessary for the evolution of pesticide resistance?
a: A population that is highly susceptible to the pesticide
Genetic variation in susceptibility to the pesticide
e: To survive bug spray, a population needs genetic variation so a few naturally tough bugs can carry on.

q: In what compartment of the ruminant stomach does fermentation primarily occur?
e: A cow's rumen is like a giant, bubbling stew pot where helpful microbes happily ferment tough grass!

q: Quorum [KWOHR-uhm] sensing in bacteria occurs when bacteria "sense" other bacteria. Which of the following triggers this phenomenon to occur?
e: Bacteria whisper by releasing tiny chemical badges called autoinducers, and once enough pile up, the crowd awakens!

q: Which of the following bird species feeds their young crop milk for the first few days after hatching?
e: Pigeon parents have a special trick: they brew rich crop milk right inside their throats to nourish their babies.

q: Which of the following scientific names correctly describes a family of plants?
e: Plant families love to dress their names with -aceae, which is why Liliaceae proudly gathers all the lilies together.

q: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and glucose are both examples of substances containing what kind of energy?
e: Like tiny wrapped gift boxes, glucose and ATP lock up chemical energy inside their bonds until your body needs a boost.

q: The lobster claw plant has red upper leaves. Which of the following pollination vectors does the lobster claw plant use?
e: Bright red leaves act like flashy welcome signs for birds, who spot the color easily and zoom in for a sweet sip!

q: Which of the following proteins is involved with prokaryotic transcription?
a: Amino acyl tRNA synthetase [ahMEEno-ASS-il tee-R.N.A. SIN-thah-tase]
e: The sigma factor acts like a trusty guide dog, leading the copying machine right to the starting line on bacterial DNA.

q: In natural systems, when a population uses the available resources at the rate equal to the resources' renewal rate, the population is said to have reached:
e: Carrying capacity is nature's perfect balance, showing the exact crowd size an ecosystem can feed without running out of snacks.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about otters?
a: Newborn otters are taken care of by their fathers only
Their dens are called holts or couches
They feed on fish, shellfish, amphibians and birds
A male otter is called a dog
e: Devoted otter moms do the heavy lifting when raising babies, so fathers definitely do not raise them all by themselves.

q: Which of the following glands contributes to thermoregulation by adjusting the resting metabolic rate?
e: Your butterfly-shaped thyroid acts like a cozy little thermostat, dialing up your body's engine speed to keep you warm.

q: In the Meselson-Stahl experiment, the mechanism for DNA replication was investigated using Escherichia coli [e-schuh-ri-KEE-uh koh-LY] as a model. E. coli was grown in medium with heavy nitrogen until all the DNA was labeled with the heavy isotope. Then, the E. coli was transferred to fresh medium with lighter nitrogen and the bacteria replicated once. The DNA was extracted from the bacteria using a density gradient to separate light-nitrogen DNA, heavy-nitrogen DNA, and light/heavy mixed DNA to decide whether replication was conservative or semiconservative. Which of the following results was predicted if replication was conservative?
a: All the DNA would be light
All of the DNA would be an intermediate density
Half of the DNA would be light, and half would be heavy
Half of the DNA would be intermediate, and half would be light
e: A conservative copy keeps the original heavy DNA completely whole, leaving half heavy and an all-new half light.

q: Which of the following is an example of simple squamous [SKWAY-mus] epithelium [eh-pih-THEEL-ee-um]?
e: Your lung lining uses these super-thin, pancake-flat cells so fresh oxygen can easily glide right into your blood.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how Pasteur attenuated the rabies virus to create an effective vaccine:
a: by treating the live virus with a weak solution of formaldehyde
by passing the rabies infection through a successive series of rabbits
by purifying the protein from the viral capsids
e: Pasteur passed the virus through rabbit after rabbit, which gently weakened the germs until they made a safe vaccine.

q: There are more possible antibodies to antigens than there are genes that code for these antibodies in the human genome. Which of the following BEST accounts for this:
a: genes mutate constantly in B cells
genes for antibodies are spliced together from different chromosomal loci
antibodies have large amounts of cross reactivity with various antigens
antibodies are only specific for certain parts of an antigen
e: Our bodies shuffle and stitch together different gene pieces from all over, like mixing puzzle pieces to build countless new defenders!

q: Apical dominance in plants means that:
a: The apical bud stimulates vertical growth
The apical bud inhibits auxin production
The apical bud stimulates floral development
The apical bud inhibits the growth of lateral buds
e: The tiptop bud acts like an ambitious leader, telling the side branches to stay asleep while it shoots upward.

q: Which of the following cellular phenomena uses double-stranded RNA with the same or similar sequence to a gene to target that gene for inhibition of transcription and translation?
e: RNA interference acts like a sneaky detective, using matching double-stranded clues to find a noisy gene and hush it up!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of substrate-level phosphorylation [FOS-for-uh-lay-shuhn] in cellular respiration?
a: ATP synthase phosphorylates [FOS-for-uh-layts] ADP during chemiosmosis [ke-mee-uh- SMOH-sis]
GDP is phosphorylated [fos-fer-uh-LAY-ted] as succinyl [SUHK-suh-nil] and CoA is converted to succinate [SUHK-suh-nayt]
e: ATP synthase acts like a spinning water wheel driven by rushing protons, so it doesn't use direct hand-to-hand chemical swaps.

q: Which of the following parts of a nerve cell acts as a resistor?
e: Ion channels act like narrow turnstiles, slowing down and controlling the rush of electric charges into the nerve cell.

q: The combined genetic information of all the members of a particular population is known as the:
e: A gene pool is like a giant community treasure chest holding every single gene that neighbors in a population share!

q: The helix-turn-helix motif is characteristic of a large group of proteins. Which of the following is a common function of the helix-turn-helix motif?
e: This clever protein shape has two little arms that reach out and snugly grab onto the grooves of DNA.

q: Which of the following types of DNA damage or distortion would be most likely to lead to an insertion or deletion during replication, resulting in a frameshift mutation?
e: Intercalation happens when a molecule squeezes between DNA rungs like an uninvited guest, confusing the copier and causing messy frameshifts.

q: Which of the following animals is most likely to be responsible for girdling a tree?
e: Hungry porcupines love munching sweet inner bark, chewing a complete ring around the tree trunk like an apple core.

q: Which of the following describes the bonds found in one molecule of water?
e: In water, oxygen shares electrons with hydrogen but hogs them slightly, creating an uneven polar covalent bond.

q: What human body cells contain H bands, Z disks and I bands?
e: Skeletal muscle cells are packed with neat, striped bands that pull together like tiny accordions to help you move!

q: What is the scientific name of the cheetah?
e: Acinonyx jubatus is the cheetah's scientific name, honoring a speedy spotted champion whose claws stay out like running cleats.

q: Which of the following organelles would you expect to be MOST active during apoptosis of the cells that contain them?
e: When a worn-out cell retires, tiny lysosomes open up like little cleanup crews to help recycle everything inside!

q: Which of the following glial cell types makes up the blood-brain barrier?
e: Star-shaped astrocytes wrap their tiny arms around blood vessels, acting like friendly security guards that keep your brain safe and sound.

q: Which of the following plant hormones is NOT correctly matched with hormone effect?
e: Cytokinins actually tell sleepy seeds to wake up and sprout, not stay resting in bed!

q: Zinc finger motifs are commonly found in proteins that do which of the following?
e: These proteins use little zinc fingers to reach out and hold onto your DNA's winding ladder.

q: Which of the following correctly describes chromatin?
a: Loosely coiled DNA and associated proteins
e: Chromatin is like your precious DNA ribbon neatly wrapped around protein spools so everything stays tidy.
