q: How do vaccines work to prevent illness? They:
a: Stop antihistamines from triggering an immune response
Alter cell surface proteins, blocking pathogens' ability to enter the cell
e: Vaccines give your immune system a safe practice drill, teaching it to build custom-made antibodies ready to tackle the real germ.

q: What is the Gray Wolf's scientific name?
e: Canis lupus is the gray wolf's grand scientific name, celebrating this magnificent wild canine of the woods.

q: In the human skull, which of the following bones does NOT contain a sinus?
e: The tiny lacrimal bone cradles your teardrops, so it simply has no room inside for a hollow, air-filled sinus pocket.

q: During meiosis, haploid cells are created from diploid parent cells. In animals, this process only takes place in:
e: Animal bodies save the special dance of meiosis strictly for reproductive organs, where they carefully craft eggs and sperm.

q: Vitamin K is important to which of the following processes?
e: When you scrape your knee, vitamin K rushes in like a tiny superhero to help your blood clot and seal the cut.

q: Indicate where action potentials are generated in a myelinated [MY-uh-luh-nay-tid] post-synaptic cell.
e: The axon hillock acts like a launch pad, gathering all the whispery signals until they are strong enough to blast an electric spark.

q: In ecology, there are two rules that identify relationships between the animal's habitat and its shape and structure. Bergmann's rule predicts that body size decreases in proximity to the equator, while Allen's rule predicts that appendages increase in size in proximity to the equator. Which of the following represents the basis for these predictions?
a: Small animals have a higher survival rate at the equator because of the dense foliage
There is less competition for food in the Arctic, so animals can grow larger
Animals with a low surface area to volume ratio can conserve heat more easily
The foundation for understanding both rules is based on Gloger's rule
e: Chilly arctic animals stay toasty because chunkier bodies have less outside skin to lose heat, keeping all their cozy warmth trapped inside.

q: Which of the following types of biological molecules is digested by trypsin:
e: Trypsin acts like a busy pair of microscopic scissors, happily snipping giant proteins apart into bite-sized pieces for your body.

q: Which of the following examples describes a postzygotic reproductive barrier that creates or enforces reproductive isolation?
a: Two closely-related species of garter snakes live in the same area, but one lives mainly in water while the other lives mainly on land
Two species of closely-related skunks have different mating seasons
Two species of closely-related snails have morphological differences that prevent successful inter-species mating
Two species of closely related equines may successfully mate to produce offspring, but the offspring is sterile
e: A postzygotic barrier happens after a baby is made, like when a horse and donkey make a mule that cannot have babies of its own.

q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of paedomorphic [ped-oh- MOOR-fik] amphibians?
e: Paedomorphic amphibians keep their cute tadpole gills as adults, but they never delay growing up on the inside to start families!

q: Which of the following is an example of a Chrysophytan [Cris-AW-fih-tan]?
e: Diatoms belong to this golden algae club, drifting through sunlit waters while wearing dazzling shells made of sparkling glass.

q: If a deer population exceeds its carrying capacity, which of the following will likely happen?
e: When too many hungry deer crowd the forest buffet, snacks run out, and the death rate sadly climbs until balance returns.

q: Bees are essential pollinators, pollinating approximately 80% of flowering agricultural crops. Why do bees pollinate?
a: It is an inadvertent product of collecting food
Bees harvest the fruits for food
It is an inadvertent product of mating
e: Bees are really just hunting for sweet snacks, but their fuzzy little coats accidentally dust flowers with pollen along the way.

q: Which of the following organisms is most likely to be a primary consumer in a lake ecosystem?
e: Tiny zooplankton drift happily through the water, munching on leafy green algae like little underwater lawnmowers!

q: Konrad Lorenz, a noted behavioral psychologist, was famous for conditioning a gaggle of geese at a particular age in their development to adopt his rubber boots as their mother. This kind of animal behavior results from which of the following?
e: Through imprinting, sweet baby geese instantly bond with the very first moving thing they see, even if it is just a muddy rainboot!

q: Which of the following is a primary function of histones H2A, H2B, H3 and H4:
a: preventing damage to DNA from ionizing radiation
holding DNA in the double helical configuration
directing the packaging of DNA into looped domains of about 300 nanometers
e: Histones act like tidy little spools, letting super-long strands of DNA wrap snugly into nucleosomes so everything fits inside the cell.

q: Which of the following hormones is derived from cholesterol?
e: Testosterone is a steroid hormone, meaning your body cleverly builds it out of cholesterol building blocks to help you grow strong.

q: How does neural transmission across a synaptic gap occur?
a: Neural impulses cause the release of neurotransmitters that diffuse across the gap
Neural impulses open potassium-gated channels, allowing sodium to move across the gap
Neural impulses travel across the gap as unidirectional electrical currents
Neural impulses travel across the gap as multidirectional electrical currents
e: When a nerve signal reaches the gap, it releases tiny neurotransmitters that float across to pass the secret note along.

q: Which of the following is true about reverse phase chromatography?
a: It is typically used for separation of proteins
e: In reverse phase chromatography, the resting material is hydrophobic, meaning it avoids water and snags other oily molecules passing by.

q: Darwin's theory of evolution stated all of the following except:
a: Those organisms best fit for their environment survive and reproduce most successfully
Species change over time through the process of natural selection
More organisms are produced than can survive, so living things compete for resources
e: Darwin knew that parents cannot pass down traits acquired during life, like getting big muscles from lifting heavy rocks.

q: During systole [SIS-tah-lee], blood is expelled from the ventricles of the heart. Which of the following is TRUE of the heart during systole?
a: The pressure in the aorta is higher than the pressure in the left ventricle
e: When the heart pumps, the atrioventricular valves snap shut tight so blood cannot splash backward into the top chambers!

q: In which of the following organisms would you most likely be able to find contractile vacuoles?
e: A tiny paramecium uses its contractile vacuole like a little bilge pump, bailing out water so it does not burst!

q: In humans, where does the organ responsible for balance reside?
e: Tucked deep inside your inner ear are tiny fluid loops that tell your brain which way is up whenever you spin around!

q: If a person had low levels of corticosteroid, which of the following would be the BEST way to test whether the adrenal glands themselves are not functioning or if it is the fault of the pituitary gland:
a: monitor the kidney for sodium excretion
measure the blood plasma for high levels of potassium
inject small amounts of corticotropin and find if the adrenals produce corticosteroids
monitor the urine for high amounts of protein and sodium
e: Injecting corticotropin acts like a wake-up call, testing if the adrenal glands can still work when given the proper signal.

q: Which of the following is NOT true when comparing the 4 steps of aerobic respiration to the 2 steps of anaerobic respiration?
a: Both utilize compounds other than glucose, such as lipids, for energy
Both recycle NADH [N-A-D-H] to NAD+ [N-A-D plus]
Both have steps occurring in the cytoplasm
e: Both processes begin with the same first step, glycolysis, so they actually both make pyruvate to get things started!

q: Gap junctions in animal cells and plasmodesmata in plant cells permit which of the following?
a: Adjacent cells to adhere strongly to each other
Secondary messengers produced in one cell to rapidly diffuse into and stimulate events in surrounding cells
The passage of connexin signals allowing coordinated cellular responses
Rapid exchange of genetic information between adjacent cells
e: These tiny tunnels let neighbor cells share quick secondary messengers, whispering important alerts to each other without delay!

q: Which of the following is true of the twenty common amino acids?
a: They contain a primary amine and secondary alcohol
They contain a primary amide and a primary alcohol
They contain a primary amine and a primary carboxyl group
They contain a secondary amine and a primary carboxyl group
e: Each amino acid carries a primary amine and a carboxyl group, like two friendly hands ready to link into proteins.

q: Which of the following molecules is most similar in structure to vitamin A?
e: Bright orange beta carotene looks like two vitamin A molecules holding hands, ready for your body to snap in half!

q: Honey doesn't spoil easily because bacteria falling into the honey are often killed. The water in the bacteria rushes out of the cell and the bacteria shrivel up because honey is a:
e: Honey is a hypertonic treat with so little water that it pulls moisture right out of bacteria until they shrivel up.

q: Which of the following statements about cystic fibrosis is NOT true?
a: It is an autosomal recessive disease
It affects the lungs, sweat glands and digestive system
It is one of the most common fatal genetic disorders in the United States
Most infants born with this disorder are unlikely to live beyond their first year
e: Thanks to amazing modern medicine, babies with cystic fibrosis can grow up and thrive for decades, far past their first birthday.

q: A patient is demonstrating loss in bone density. Which of the following hormones would be most useful in treating this symptom?
e: Calcitonin acts like a busy builder, packing calcium straight into your bones to keep them sturdy and strong.

q: Which of the following metallic elements can be found in hemoglobin?
e: Hemoglobin holds a tiny bit of iron at its heart to catch oxygen and carry it happily all over your body!

q: Which of the following MOST likely occurs during speciation (read as: spee-cee-A-tion):
e: During speciation, reproductive isolation keeps groups apart so they stop mating and eventually become two distinct new species.

q: Which of the following plant hormones is manufactured primarily in the shoot tips, in embryos, and in parts of developing flowers and seeds?
e: Tiny sprout tips make auxins to stretch up tall and reach toward the warm, welcoming sunshine.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of old growth forests?
a: All trees are roughly the same age
Ground cover is low in organic matter
e: Over hundreds of quiet years, fallen leaves help ancient soil settle into neat, well-defined layers like a giant earthy cake.

q: What material typically constitutes the cell wall in fungi?
e: Mushrooms build their sturdy little walls out of chitin, the very same tough stuff that coats crunchy beetle shells.

q: What component of the nephron establishes and maintains a salt gradient used to concentrate urine?
e: The Loop of Henle swoops down like a tiny rollercoaster, cleverly trapping salt to help your kidneys save water.

q: A Paramecium [par-uh-MEE-see-uhm] lives in fresh water and has a contractile vacuole [kuhn-TRAK-tl VAK-yoo-ohl] that allows it to regularly expel excess water that enters its cell. Which of the following is correct?
a: The inside of the cell is hypertonic compared to the outside of the cell, so water enters the cell through osmosis
The inside of the cell is hypotonic to the outside of the cell, so water enters the cell through osmosis
The inside and outside of the cell are isotonic, but water enters the cell as the Paramecium swims around
The cellular processes of the Paramecium produce a lot of excess water, so it needs to get rid of the extra water
e: Because the cell is hypotonic to the pond water, extra water rushes inside, forcing the little critter to bail it out.

q: Which of the following amino acids is encoded by a single codon?
e: While other protein building blocks share several code words, methionine is unique because it listens to just one single genetic codon.

q: Which of the following is true regarding osmoregulation in a freshwater fish?
a: Osmotic water loss occurs over body surface and via gills
Nitrogenous wastes are excreted primarily in the form of uric acid
Copious amount of urine hypotonic to the blood is excreted
Excess salt is excreted from gills
e: Freshwater fish constantly soak up pond water, so they stay balanced by peeing out huge puddles of super-watery urine.

q: Where is the Gluteus Maximus muscle located?
e: That mighty gluteus maximus muscle is in your butt, helping you run, leap, and sit down for storytime!

q: You are surfing at the beach and see a shark nearby, activating your vertebrate stress response. Levels of which of the following would decrease during this response?
e: When a shark startles you, your body drops insulin levels so plenty of sugary fuel stays in your blood for swimming fast.

q: Which of the following groups of protists is most closely related to plants?
e: Red algae are like ancient cousins to leafy plants, sharing special sunlight-catching traits that other protists simply do not have.

q: Which of the following is true of genetic mutations?
a: They are always harmful and usually hurt the organism
They are always beneficial and frequently help the organism adapt to the environment
They are not natural and should not happen unless something goes wrong
They can be harmful, helpful, or have no effect on the organism
e: Nature loves surprises, so a tiny gene change can help an animal, cause a problem, or do nothing at all.

q: If you were a farmer that wanted to promote the ripening of your fruit crop, which of the following hormones would be best to use?
e: Ethylene is a friendly gas that whispers to hard green fruit, telling each piece it is time to turn sweet and soft.

q: Which of the following is NOT a seedless, vascular plant?
e: Unlike ferns, humble little liverworts lack internal water pipes, which makes them non-vascular wanderers of the forest floor.

q: Grasses provide an example of a root system that is best described as which of the following?
e: Grasses are monocots that spread out a tangled, web-like net of fibrous roots to hug the dirt tight.

q: Which of the following enzymes is unique to gluconeogenesis [gloo-koh-nee-uh-JEN-uh-sis]?
e: PEP carboxykinase has the special one-way job of building fresh sugar, so you only find it in gluconeogenesis.

q: Which process will almost certainly result in genetic variation of offspring?
e: When fertilization joins two parent cells, their genes shuffle together to create a brand-new, completely unique baby.

q: Robert Hooke coined the term `cell' mostly because of:
a: his observations of red blood cells
his analysis of hundreds of different protozoans
his readings of the works of other early microscopists
e: Peeking at cork bark under his microscope, Robert Hooke thought the tiny boxy spaces looked just like little monk rooms.

q: Which of the following situations might cause disruptive selection to occur in a population of seed-eating finches on an island?
a: A hurricane that wipes out plants that produce medium-sized seeds
A hurricane that wipes out plants that produce small and large seeds
A hurricane that wipes out plants that produce small seeds
A hurricane that reduces equally plants that produce all sizes of seeds
e: Losing medium seeds splits the flock, helping birds with tiny or huge beaks while leaving middle-sized beaks hungry.

q: Which of the following eye adaptations allows nocturnal animals to see better in dim light when compared to diurnal animals?
a: Relatively higher numbers of cone cells
Presence of a tapetum [tuh-pee-tum] that reflects rather than absorbs light
Chemically distinctive vitreous humor that better supports the retina
A less convex lens that facilities an ideal focal length in dim light
e: The shiny tapetum acts like a built-in mirror, bouncing dim moonlight across the eye so night critters can see.

q: Which of the following organisms would use the highest percentage of its energy budget for homeostatic regulation?
e: A warm-blooded desert bird spends heaps of its daily energy battling scorching heat just to keep its body temperature steady.

q: Which of the following is NOT an adaptation for flight in birds?
e: Male birds actually pack a matching pair of testes inside, so having just one isn't their clever secret for soaring high.

q: What kind of behavior causes bees to visit flowers to collect nectar and pollen?
e: Tiny bees are born already knowing the sweet dance of finding flowers, no classroom lessons required!

q: A sperm cell is found to have 18 chromosomes. How many molecules of DNA were present during Metaphase I of the cell cycle?
e: The starting cell doubled its 36 chromosomes into 72 DNA strands, getting all dressed up before the grand dividing dance.

q: Which of the following brain regions is incorrectly matched with its function?
a: Hippocampus [hip-uh-KAM-puhs] allows two brain hemispheres to communicate with each other
e: The seahorse-shaped hippocampus saves your favorite memories, leaving bridge-building between brain sides to someone else.

q: Which of the following molecules are NOT covalently attached to proteins as post-translational modifications?
a: Ions such as Ca+2 and Mg+2
e: Busy metal ions just visit proteins for a quick chat, never gluing themselves down with permanent chemical bonds.

q: After a volcanic eruption wipes out the organisms on an island, which of the following would be the first to recolonize?
e: Brave little grass seeds can ride the gentle wind across the sea, landing first to bring green life back to rocky ash.

q: Which of the following substances is transported into cells via carrier-assisted transport?
e: Charged sodium ions cannot slip through walls alone, so friendly helper proteins carry them safely inside.

q: In the case of disruptive selection on tail length in monkeys, which of the following would you expect?
e: Nature favors super short or super long tails here, leaving hardly any room for everyday medium-tailed monkeys.

q: Electroporation of a cell enables which of the following?
a: Polar molecules to pass through the plasma membrane
Glucose to escape the plasma membrane
Polar molecules to intercalate into the plasma membrane [in-TUR-kuh-layt]
Non-polar molecules to escape the plasma membrane
e: A tiny spark zaps open microscopic gates in the oily cell wall, letting watery polar molecules slip right in.

q: In green plants, energy is stored mainly in which of the following forms?
e: Plants bundle their extra sugary sunshine into cozy pantry packages called starch, saving snacks for a cloudy day.

q: Cephalopods belong to which of the following groups?
e: Clever squids and octopuses belong to the mollusk family, making them secret squishy cousins to snails and clams!

q: Which of the following is another name for the "Poecilotheria Metallica Tarantula"?
e: This dazzling bright blue spider is nicknamed the Gooty tarantula after the town in India where it was discovered.

q: Which of the following is NOT a point mutation?
e: While point mutations swap just one tiny letter, an inversion flips a whole giant sentence of DNA upside down.

q: During starvation, muscles convert most of the amino acids released from muscle breakdown to what two specific amino acids for use in gluconeogenesis [gloo-koh-nee-uh-JEN-uh-sis]?
e: Hungry muscles transform their spare building blocks into alanine and glutamine, shipping them off to make fresh sugar.

q: Which of the following is true regarding the neural crest cells in the amphibian embryo?
a: They induce formation of the notochord
They develop into the main sections of the brain
They produce cells that migrate to form teeth and skull bones in the embryo
They roll up and form the neural tube
e: These adventurous young cells travel across the growing baby, shaping sturdy skull bones and chompers along the way.

q: How many known living species of hyenas are there?
e: Today, exactly four hyena species roam our wild world, including the famous spotted hyena and the shy aardwolf!

q: Which of the following is a primary target of certain HIV drugs, such as AZT, specifically because HIV is a retrovirus:
e: The virus uses reverse transcriptase to rewrite its recipe backwards into DNA, making that copy machine the best target to stop.

q: Which of the following is true regarding plant ground tissue?
a: Parenchyma [puh-RENG-kuh-muh] is mostly responsible for structural support
Collenchyma [kuh-LENG-kuh-muh] consists of dead cells with thick cell walls
Sclerenchyma [skli-RENG-kuh-muh] is the most lignified type of ground tissue
Sclerenchyma cells can adapt to stress conditions at maturity
e: Sclerenchyma cells pack their walls with tough lignin, acting like the plant's rigid wooden armor to keep it standing tall.

q: Which of the following animals possess two circuits of blood flow, the pulmocutaneous [POOL-moh-kyoo-tay-NEE-uhs] and systemic?
e: Wet little salamanders send blood to their lungs and moist skin, using a special circuit to breathe.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of the negative effects of bioaccumulation of toxins in the environment?
a: The thinning of bird eggshells due to DDT
Inedibility of oysters due to their filter feeding on naturally occurring red tide algae
Birth defects in babies exposed to Accutane in utero
Inedibility of fish due to mercury content
e: Accutane is a medicine taken directly by a patient, not a wild poison slowly building up across an outdoor food chain.

q: Heartwood and sapwood consist of which of the following?
e: Inside a growing tree, old and new wood team up as secondary xylem, happily carrying water upward and keeping the giant standing tall.

q: Progesterone levels reach a peak at which of the following points of the human menstrual cycle?
e: In the secretory phase, progesterone shoots to the top, bustling around like a caring builder to make the womb cozy and ready.

q: In the human digestive system, nutrient absorption predominantly occurs in which of the following?
e: The duodenum and jejunum work like busy little sponge buddies, soaking up all the yummy nutrients from your lunch.

q: Which of the following best describes the conversion of 2PG to PEP in glycolysis [glye-KAWL- eh-sis]?
e: To make PEP, a tiny molecular scissor snips a carbon-oxygen bond, popping off water like a stray button!

q: Which of the following is NOT part of initiation during translation?
a: Binding of a small ribosomal subunit to mRNA and initiator tRNA
e: A TATA box belongs to transcription on DNA, so it sits out when translation starts building a protein.

q: What type of phagocytic cell can primarily be found under mucosal [myoo-KOH-sul] surfaces and plays a primary role in responding to multicellular pathogens?
e: Eosinophils are brave little defenders stationed in our moist linings, ready to swarm giant invading worms!

q: Which of the following is TRUE:
a: chimpanzees are an ancestor of Homo sapiens
bipedal motion dominated hominoid ancestors by about 30 million years ago
humans and modern apes have a common ancestor
Neanderthals were ancestors to modern humans
e: Humans and modern apes are like cousins who share a wonderful ancient grandparent from millions of years ago.

q: Which of the following is MOST directly involved in the motility and intercellular signaling in T-cells:
e: Filamentous actin acts like tiny muscles and tracks, helping T-cells crawl along and whisper signals to their neighbors.

q: Which of the following roles does creatine play in the human body?
e: Creatine acts like a mini battery pack in your muscles, giving them a fast burst of energy when you sprint!

q: Which of the following are examples of asexual reproduction?
e: Fragmentation, budding, and binary fission let single parents make mini copies of themselves without needing a partner.

q: While hiking in Arizona, you come over a rise, hear a rattling sound and see a western diamondback rattlesnake coiled and ready to strike. Indicate which of the following physiological responses would NOT occur in you?
a: Gluconeogenesis would occur in the liver
Blood vessels in the gut and skin would constrict
Heart rate and blood pressure would increase
Adipose tissue would release fatty acids to the blood stream
e: A sudden snake fright demands instant sugar from stores, so the slow process of gluconeogenesis waits for later.

q: Which of the following is definitely known about Australopithecines [aw-stral-oh-PITH-eh-seens]?
a: They were 2 meters tall, on average
e: Long ago, australopithecines proudly stepped out on two legs, walking upright across the grassy plains.

q: The taxonomic class Myxini [MIK-suh-nee] contains which of the following fish?
e: Hagfish belong to class Myxini, swimming deep in the ocean and making glorious clouds of slime!

q: Which of the following would BEST describe the quaternary structure of collagen:
e: Collagen weaves together like super-strong ropes, giving it a fibrous shape that holds our bodies together.

q: Which of the following choices is NOT a source of new genetic combinations?
e: Mitosis is a copycat machine, making identical twin cells rather than mixing up any new genetic combinations.

q: Within the human forebrain, which of the following structures does not belong to the telencephalon [tel-en-SEF-uh-lon] ?
e: The hardworking hypothalamus lives in the diencephalon neighborhood, so it is not part of the telencephalon.

q: Which of the following types of animal viruses is responsible for hepatitis C?
e: Hepatitis C belongs to the sneaky Flavivirus family, hiding inside a tiny shell to cause liver mischief.

q: The toxin from the death cap mushroom is alpha-amanitin. This toxin primarily binds and inhibits RNA polymerase [POL-uh-muh-rays] II. Transcription of which of the following types of RNA would be most impacted by poisoning with alpha-amanitin?
e: RNA polymerase two writes the recipes called mRNA, so this mushroom toxin halts mRNA in its tracks!

q: In eukaryotic cells, which of the following metabolic reactions does NOT occur within the mitochondrion?
e: Glycolysis happens right out in the open cytoplasm, never stepping foot inside the bustling mitochondrion.

q: Which of the following is NOT a response of liver cells to glucagon?
a: Increase of release of calcium ions
e: Glucagon tells the liver to share its stored energy, which shuts down fat synthesis instead of increasing it.

q: Which of the following mammal species is usually considered diurnal [dy-UR-nl]?
e: While other critters love sneaking under the moon, the cheerful fox squirrel spends sunny days scampering up trees to hide acorns!

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding juvenile hormone (JH) in the silkworm moth as it pertains to the hormonal control of insect metamorphosis?
a: JH is produced by the prothoracic [proh-tha-RAS-ik] gland
Levels of JH are higher in first instar larvae [LAHR-vee] relative to levels in fifth instar larvae
Pupae [PYOO-pee] have little to no JH
The interplay of ecdysone [EK-duh-sohn] and JH is important to the molting process
e: Juvenile hormone is actually cooked up near the brain by the corpora allata, leaving the prothoracic gland to make a different molting chemical.

q: Which of the following BEST explains how cyclic AMP can cause so many different intracellular responses in a mammalian cell:
a: it is produced in large quantities
it migrates to the DNA where it binds to a variety of histones
it activates a wide variety of specific protein kinases
it prevents the activation of other hormonal signals
e: Like a busy conductor tapping different musicians, cyclic AMP turns on various helper proteins called kinases that get cell chores dancing!

q: Which of the following correctly explains why fish cannot breathe outside of water?
a: Air contains less oxygen than water
Their gas exchange systems are tuned to dissolved oxygen
Air provides more structural support to the fish
e: Without water to float them open, a fish’s delicate gills stick together and collapse like wet tissue paper, blocking fresh oxygen.

q: Aposematic coloration allows an organism to signal which of the following?
e: Bright, flashy warning colors act like nature’s neon sign, shouting to hungry predators that this little critter tastes horribly toxic!

q: Which of the following is the form of highly condensed chromatin that is not transcribable in its present form and typical of the type of chromatin visible in the light microscope when the cell is in interphase:
e: Heterochromatin is packed together as tight as a rolled-up sleeping bag, keeping its secret genetic instructions hidden away and unreadable.

q: Members of the order Gymnophiona (read as: jim-noh-FYOH- nah), otherwise known as Caecilians (read as: si-SIL-yahns), do NOT have which of the following?
e: These wiggly, worm-like amphibians burrow underground without needing any legs at all, happily sliding through the dirt!

q: Sutures are an example of what type of joint?
e: Sutures lock your skull bones together like interlocking puzzle pieces, forming completely immovable joints that keep your brain safe and snug.

q: Which of these animals is NOT a lizard?
e: While the tuatara looks like a scaly lizard, it is an ancient survivor from its very own unique reptile family.

q: A plant loses the greatest amount of water through what structures?
e: Leaves are covered in microscopic breathing mouths called stomata, and when they open wide, most of the plant’s water floats away!

q: Which of the following is the highest level of structural organization in myoglobin:
e: Since myoglobin is just one single protein strand folded into a neat three-dimensional ball, its highest structure is tertiary.

q: Which of the following fossils is representative of the transition from fish to tetrapods?
e: Tiktaalik is the famous ancient "fishapod" that used sturdy wrist-like fins to do push-ups, showing how swimming fish first stepped onto land!

q: Which of the following is NOT a blood vessel located in the human head or neck:
e: While your neck has big jugular veins and carotid arteries, nature never invented any blood vessel called a jugular artery!

q: Which of the following chemical bonds does NOT correctly characterize the interaction between two molecules?
a: Peptide bond: amino acid to amino acid
e: Codons and anticodons hold hands using gentle, temporary hydrogen bonds, not super-strong permanent covalent bonds, so they can easily let go.

q: How many fused rings does the carbon skeleton of steroids have?
e: Every steroid molecule builds its sturdy little skeleton out of four carbon rings locked tightly together side by side.

q: A flower is purple in color, contains no nectar, and has an irregular shape. Which of the following is the most likely pollinator of this plant?
e: Without sweet nectar, this weird purple bloom disguises itself as rotting meat to fool stink-loving flesh flies into visiting!

q: Hemolymph (read as; HEE-moh-lim(p)f) in the insect Epicauta vittata (read as: eh-pee-KOH-tah vee-TAH-tah) has all of the following functions, EXCEPT:
e: Bug blood carries yummy food and water, but insects breathe through special air tubes, so their hemolymph doesn't carry oxygen.

q: The black fur allele B (read as: big b), is dominant over the white fur allele b (read as: little b). Two mice with black fur mate, producing four offspring: one is white and three are black. What are the likely genotypes of the two parents?
e: To surprise everyone with a white baby, both black-furred mouse parents had to secretly carry a hidden white gene, making them both Bb!

q: In a human, breathing air with too much carbon dioxide would lead to all of the following except:
a: A reduction in oxygen carrying capacity
A decrease in oxygen affinity for hemoglobin
A rightward shift of the oxygen equilibrium curve
e: Extra carbon dioxide helps blood drop off oxygen faster, but it doesn’t lower the total amount of oxygen hemoglobin can carry.

q: HIV primarily targets CD4-positive lymphocytes. Which of the following best describes the normal function of these cells?
a: Receive presented antigens and stimulate other cells
Send signals to infected cells to apoptose [ay-POP-tows]
e: These friendly helper cells act like cheerleaders, spotting suspicious germ clues and exciting the rest of the immune army into action!

q: When using a light microscope to view a stained cross section of a dorsal root ganglion, which of the following structures are you most likely to see?
e: Inside this cozy nerve hub, round cell bodies of sensory neurons gather together, waiting to hear what your skin touches next!

q: When two pyrimidine [py-RIM-i-deen] bases are adjacent on a DNA strand, exposure to UV light will commonly lead to formation of a cyclobutane ring between them, resulting in a bulky lesion in the DNA. The normal replicative polymerases [pol-uh-muh- RAYS-uhs] cannot use this as a template, and the lesion often results in mutation if it cannot be repaired. Which of the following is an example of this lesion formed by UV exposure of neighboring pyrimidines [py-RIM-i-deens]?
e: Harsh sunlight glues twin DNA rungs into a thymine dimer, leaving a bumpy little knot that stops cell machinery in its tracks.

q: What phylum [FYE- lum] of animals contains organisms that do not possess tissues?
e: Gentle sea sponges belong to Porifera, living peacefully on the ocean floor as simple clusters of cells without any true tissues.

q: In which of the following environments would a plant exhibiting CAM photosynthesis most likely be found?
e: Clever desert plants save water with CAM tricks, opening their pores only in cool night breezes to thrive in dry, arid homes.

q: Honeybees leave the hive to find food. Upon finding food, honeybees return to the hive and dance to tell others how to find the food. This behavior is an example of:
e: Honeybees rely on visual communication, eagerly watching a sister's cheerful wiggle dance to learn the secret path to sweet flowers.

q: Which of the following is NOT a seedless plant?
e: Unlike mossy seedless wanderers, bright St. John's wort sprouts sunny yellow petals that wrap up real seeds for the next generation.

q: Which of the following animals does not possess an amniotic [am-nee-AW-tic] membrane at any stage of development?
e: Salamanders are amphibians that lay jelly eggs in water, skipping the cozy amniotic blanket wrapped around baby lizards and warm mammals.

q: Which of the following would be least likely to be a life history trait of an r-selected organism?
e: Speedy r-selected critters rush to raise lots of babies, so they never develop the strong competitive ability needed for tough turf wars.

q: Which of the following statements about the lone star tick is true?
a: It feeds on humans, dogs, and cats
e: This bold lone star tick is never picky, happily hitching a ride on humans, dogs, and cats for an unwelcome meal.

q: Which of the following is NOT an energy source for active transport across a membrane?
a: Electrochemical gradient of a different molecule
e: Cell pumps run on batteries like ATP, but Ras proteins are busy talkers, not energy sources.

q: Bacteria are able to become resistant to antibiotics by increasing their genetic variability through all of the following mechanisms EXCEPT:
e: Binary fission simply splits a bacterium into identical twins, which cannot introduce any fresh genetic surprises to help it survive.

q: Which of the following is a model of enzyme action?
e: In the induced fit model, a friendly enzyme shifts its shape to give its chemical visitor a snug, custom hug.

q: Which of the following was first proposed by Peter Mitchell as a potential energy ion gradient across a selectively permeable membrane that is responsible for the production of ATP:
e: Chemiosmosis lets charged particles tumble through a membrane like water over a dam, spinning cellular motors to build energetic ATP.

q: Bacteria use which of the following mechanisms during quorum [KWOHR-uhm] sensing?
e: Clever bacteria whisper tiny chemical signals called autoinducers, counting their crowd before springing into action together.

q: Which of the following best describes a lysogenic cell?
a: It is immune to viral infection
It is actively producing viral particles
e: A lysogenic cell acts like a gentle host, letting a sleeping viral guest called a prophage snooze quietly inside its DNA.

q: What mammalian characteristic do Echidnas [eh-KID-nahs] lack?
e: Quirky echidnas are mammals that produce milk, but they lack nipples, so babies must lap milk straight off mama's skin.

q: According to the 3 domain system of classification with the 3 domains being, Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya, which of the following would be LEAST likely to belong to the domain Bacteria:
e: Super-hot boiling springs usually belong to hardy Archaea, making non-nucleated thermophiles the rarest guests among everyday bacteria.

q: In a particular bird population, individuals that lay too many or too few eggs are less likely to survive and reproduce. Which of the following terms best describes this pattern of natural selection?
e: Nature keeps baby birds safe through stabilizing selection, favoring just the right nest size rather than too many or too few.

q: In horses, the genotype little-B little-B causes early embryonic lethality. The A locus behaves as a classic Mendelian gene. If two horses with identical genotypes AaBb [big-A, little-A, big-B, little-B] mate, what is the expected phenotypic ratio of their offspring?
a: 9:3:3:1 [read as nine to three to three to one]
3:1:1 [read as three to one to one]
9:3:1 [read as nine to three to one]
e: Because double-b baby horses do not survive, only the classic A gene shows through in a tidy three-to-one family portrait.

q: Which disease-causing agent is NOT correctly matched to the disease it causes?
a: Plasmodium falciparum (read as: plahz-ME-dee-uhm fahl-SI-pah-ruhm) - Dengue hemorrhagic fever
Rickettsia rickettsii (read as: ri-KEHT-see-ah ri-KEHT-see) - Rocky Mountain spotted fever
Borrelia burgdorferi (read as: boh-REHL-ee-ah boorg-DOHR-feh-ree) - Lyme disease
Trypanosoma brucei (read as: try-pah-noh-SE-mah BROOH-sey) - Human African sleeping sickness
e: Plasmodium falciparum causes malaria instead of Dengue fever, making it the odd bug out in this sickness lineup.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of northern elephant seals?
a: They are the largest phocids (read as: FOH-sids) in the Northern Hemisphere
They do not eat on land
They dive to depths of 1,000 to 2,500 feet underwater
e: Big boy elephant seals pick so many beach brawls that they wear out faster, meaning mama seals actually live longer!

q: Assume you would like to isolate a specific membrane protein from a cell. How could you best remove the protein from the membrane?
a: Disrupt the lipid bilayer with detergents
Grind the cells using a pestle
Stain the target protein with fluorescing antibodies
Centrifuge the cells to separate the lipid bilayer from other cellular components
e: Just like dish soap washes grease off a plate, gentle detergents dissolve the cell's oily skin to set trapped proteins free.

q: What human organ utilizes the most glucose in the body?
e: Your busy brain is a sweet tooth that gobbles up more sugar power than any other organ just to keep thinking!

q: Which of the following is an example of a covalent bond or bonds?
a: The bond between two adjacent amino acids in a polypeptide chain
The bond between a tRNA anticodon and an mRNA codon
The bonds between the large subunit and the small subunit of the ribosome [RY-buh-sohm]
The bonds between the small ribosomal subunit and the mRNA
e: Amino acids link hands with super-strong covalent bonds, sharing electrons to build sturdy protein chains like unbreakable necklaces.

q: TSH causes the thyroid to produce more T3. When T3 rises, it flows through the blood to the brain to decrease the release of TSH. Which of the following is the MOST accurate and common term for this physiological phenomenon:
e: Like a thermostat turning off the heat when it gets cozy, negative feedback tells the brain to stop making hormones.

q: Which of the following animals is considered a keystone species of the kelp forests of the Aleutian [uh-LOO-shuhn] Islands ecosystem?
e: Fluffy sea otters protect the giant seaweed forests by munching on greedy sea urchins that try to chew everything down.

q: Which of the following is NOT true in humans:
a: trisomy X originates from a nondisjunction
albumin is produced by the liver
the spleen produces red blood cells in the fetus
e: While most helper enzymes wear protein coats, clever little RNA molecules can act like busy enzymes, too.

q: Which of the following is the most common term for an area of primitive cells in plants where active cell division occurs:
e: At the tip of every sprout, a lively little factory called a meristem divides non-stop to help plants reach the sky!

q: Which of the following does the enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase [uh-mee-noh-AS-il T-R-N-A SIN-thuh-tays] catalyze?
a: Base-pairing between the tRNA and the mRNA
Transfer of the amino acid from the tRNA to form a peptide bond
Charging of a tRNA with an amino acid
e: This helpful matchmaker enzyme snaps the right amino acid onto its little tRNA delivery truck, charging it up for work.

q: Raspberry is an aggregate fruit, meaning that it develops from which of the following?
a: A single carpel of one flower
e: A sweet raspberry forms when many carpels inside a single flower join hands to make one bumpy berry cluster!

q: Which of the following structures would have been most likely absent from the last shared common ancestor of osteichthyans [os-tee-IK-thee-uhns] and chondrichthyans [kan-DRIK-thee-ez]?
e: Their ancient fish grandpa swam without a swim bladder, a handy balloon that bony fish invented much later!

q: In which of the following organ systems do the tonsils primarily function?
e: Sitting like twin castle guards in your throat, tonsils belong to the lymphatic system to trap sneaky germs.

q: Blood albumin is most directly involved with:
e: Albumin acts like a sponge in your blood, balancing water levels through osmoregulation so fluids stay right where they belong.

q: The absence of which of the following transcript components would decrease eukaryotic [yoo-KAR-ee-oh-tik] translational initiation?
e: Without its poly(A) tail, a gene message cannot properly invite the cell to start translation.

q: During which of the following phases of an action potential do voltage-gated sodium channels begin to close?
e: When an electric nerve wave crashes down during the falling phase, the tiny sodium doors slam shut to reset.

q: The majority of speciation [spee-see-AY-shun] occurs under which of the following circumstances?
e: When critters get separated by rivers or mountains, they slowly change into brand new species on their own cozy adventures.

q: Which of the following pairs of echinoderms [ih-KY-nuh-durms] have respiratory structures that could be characterized as lungs rather than gills, since they are formed from invaginations of the body surface?
e: Sea cucumbers and brittle stars breathe through hidden body pockets tucked inside, acting just like tiny underwater lungs!

q: All Homo sapiens are thought to share a common matrilineage. What genetic information has been used as key evidence for this shared matrilineage?
e: Mothers pass their special mitochondrial DNA directly to their babies like a family heirloom that traces back through history.

q: Which of the following is missing in bryophytes and is an evolutionary advancement of higher plants:
e: Little mosses stay short because they lack vascular plumbing pipes to pump water up toward the sunshine!

q: Which of the following organisms probably uses PEP carboxylase to capture carbon dioxide and keep stomata closed during the day?
e: Thirsty desert plants like aloe vera lock their pores all day, using PEP carboxylase to catch carbon at night instead!

q: Which of the following insect orders is characterized by the beak or stylet arising from the posterior part of the head and extending along the insect's sternum?
e: Tiny Homoptera bugs wear their pointy drinking straw tucked way back under their chins, resting neatly along their chests.

q: Ferredoxin is an electron-transfer protein that contains which of the following?
e: Ferredoxin carries busy little electrons using a cozy cluster of iron and sulfur atoms, passing energy along like a sparkling secret.

q: Which of the following plant hormones play a role in fruit ripening?
e: Gibberellins act like magical growth whisperers, nudging green fruits to swell up, ripen, and get ready for a sweet picnic.

q: The grouping of modern humans and chimpanzees forms which of the following types of groups?
e: Grouping just chimps and humans is polyphyletic because it leaves out their shared relatives, like snapping a photo without the whole family tree!

q: Which of the following compounds acts as an activator protein for the lactose operon in Escherichia (read as: ehsh-eh-RIK-ee-ah) coli?
e: A helpful protein called CAP flips the switch, cheering the cell on to digest lactose whenever it needs a tasty sugar snack.

q: In active meiosis, new genetic combinations can arise in two different ways. Which of the following is the first stage in which there could be genetic recombination?
e: In prophase one, chromosomes cozy up and swap genetic trading cards, creating brand-new combinations before the big cell-division dance even begins.

q: Which of the following types of fatty acids would alpha linolenic or all cis-9,12,15-Octadecatrienoic (read as: octa-deca-tri-en-oh-ick) acid most commonly be classified:
e: When you count carbon steps from the tail end, the very first double bond sits at number three, making it an omega-three!

q: Which of the following is an insertion of the human biceps femoris muscle:
a: ventral portion of the head of the femur
lateral sides of the head of the tibia
e: Your mighty biceps femoris muscle anchors to the outer side of your shinbone's head, helping your knee bend for every joyful jump.

q: A certain flower has a large amount of nectar, is colored red, and has no fragrance. Which of the following pollination vectors did it evolve to exploit?
e: Feathered birds love bright red petals and slurp lots of sweet nectar, but they never mind if a flower has no smell!

q: Which of the following methods was used to determine the 3D structure of hemoglobin?
e: Scientists shone clever X-rays through a hemoglobin crystal, watching the bounced beams reveal its twisty three-dimensional shape like an invisible puzzle.

q: The organisms that form arbuscular mycorrhizae are part of what group of fungi?
e: Friendly glomeromycetes reach into plant roots with tiny, tree-like fungal fingers, sharing soil goodies in a wonderful underground friendship.

q: Which of the following organisms is NOT an autotroph?
e: Plants and green bacteria make their own meals, but a hungry mosquito must buzz around hunting others for its lunch.

q: If you have a white horse mate with a white horse that has many spots called leopard spots and half of their offspring have a little bit of leopard spotting, which of the following is your likely conclusion about the leopard-spotting allele?
e: When spotting is incompletely dominant, the genes blend like paints, giving baby foals just a gentle sprinkle of spots.

q: Your body has approximately one million B cells and ten million different T cells. A gram-negative bacterium enters your body and one of your B cells binds to the bacterium via the BCR recognizing the LPS. Which of the following will happen next?
a: The virus will enter the B cell
Similar T cells will be destroyed
The B cell will be destroyed
e: Once this brave B cell catches the invader, it quickly multiplies into a whole army of defenders to save the day!

q: A type of albinism in the Hopi Native American population is caused by mutation of the OCA2 gene. If the dominant form of the gene gives a person normal pigmentation, then which of the following genotypes would result in albinism?
e: To show albinism, a child needs two copies of the quiet, mutated gene, making their genotype homozygous recessive.

q: Cloning a gene into a plasmid often requires you to amplify the target DNA sequence, then digest and paste the target sequence into the plasmid. Several purified enzymes are important in this process. Which of the following enzymes would act LAST in the cloning process?
e: After DNA pieces are copied and cut to size, sticky ligase arrives last like molecular glue to seal everything tight.

q: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of eudicots [yoo-DY- kots]?
a: Flower parts in multiples of 4 or 5
e: Eudicot pollen grains proudly show off three tiny grooves, so having just one single opening belongs to other flower families instead.

q: Which of the following instruments would be used to perform a polymerase chain reaction in a molecular biology lab?
e: A thermocycler acts like a cozy little oven and cooler, cycling temperatures up and down so DNA copies can multiply fast.

q: Whales and dolphins are most closely related to which of the following groups of mammals?
e: Believe it or not, swimming whales share their closest family branch with even-toed hoofed critters like cheerful hippos and deer!

q: Which of the following is NOT in the insect group Apterygota (read as: ahp-teh-ri-GE-tah)?
e: Apterygota bugs are naturally wingless, but speedy cockroaches grow wings, which boots them out of that flightless club.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why a single base substitution in a gene-coding region for amino acids will sometimes lead to no change in amino acid sequence:
a: all nucleotides are subject to the same mutation rate
some nucleotide bases are covalently joined by stronger bonds
the code is degenerate with more than one triplet coding for the same amino acid
some amino acids act in the same fashion in determining the tertiary structure of a protein
e: Life's recipe book has multiple spellings for the same ingredient, so a tiny typo still makes the exact same protein!

q: Which of the following hormones is a precursor of both estrogen and testosterone?
e: Think of DHEA as a handy starter block that your body reshapes into both estrogen and testosterone.

q: Which of the following muscles adducts and rotates the scapula and tilts the chin?
e: Your trusty trapezius muscle acts like a cape across your back, proudly tilting your chin up and moving your shoulder blades!

q: Which of the following statements is true of root hairs?
a: They increase the surface area of the root for absorption of water
They are located in each stomate on the root
They are found on both stems and roots
They are involved in mechanical stabilization of the plant
e: Tiny root hairs spread out like millions of fuzzy straws, giving thirsty plants way more surface area to slurp up water!

q: As could be detected clinically during a functional magnetic resonance image, which of the following parts of the brain would be activated when a person is faced with a fearful situation?
e: Meet the amygdala, your brain's watchful little alarm bell that instantly lights up whenever something feels spooky.

q: Which of the following best explains the property of TAQ polymerase [tak pol-UH-muh-rays] that makes it ideal for use in PCR reactions?
a: It is resistant to mechanical perturbation
It can remain stable at a variety of pH levels
It can be used in low concentrations
e: Taq polymerase loves extreme heat and never melts, making it the perfect tough little helper for copying warm DNA!

q: Which of the following is not a medically relevant difference between eukaryotic cells and bacterial cells?
a: Presence of peptidoglycan layer in bacteria
e: Bacteria and human cells actually share the exact same genetic language, so medicine cannot use the code to tell them apart.

q: Maple syrup is extracted from maple trees by tapping what part of the plant?
e: Sweet maple sap flows upward through inner tree pipes called xylem, right where thirsty tappers collect it!

q: Muscle fibers can be classified as slow, intermediate, or fast. Which of the following is NOT true regarding fast muscle fibers?
a: They are found in higher relative abundance in world class sprinters versus world class marathoners
They have the highest mitochondrial density
The primary pathway for ATP production is fermentation
e: Fast muscle fibers choose quick bursts over lots of powerhouses, meaning they actually have the fewest mitochondria around!

q: Melissa synthesizes a DNA plasmid in which expression of green fluorescent protein is under the lac [lack] promoter and lacI [lack-EYE] is upstream of the promoter. Which of the following small molecules can she add to bacteria expressing this plasmid to induce expression of green fluorescent protein?
e: Allolactose gently unhooks the brakes on bacterial DNA, happily switching on the instructions to glow green!

q: Darwin's finches differ from other finches in the size and shape of their beaks. Which of the following factors has been identified as the major influence on the development of the differing beaks?
e: Each finch grew a custom beak shaped like a handy tool just to crack open its own favorite island snack!

q: Which of the following proteins would likely be synthesized by a cytosolic ribosome instead of an ER-bound ribosome?
e: Because actin stays inside to build the cell's skeleton, floating cytosolic ribosomes can easily craft it right in the fluid.

q: Which of the following terms best describes humans?
e: Humans are viviparous because mothers give birth to living, wiggling babies rather than laying eggs in a nest.

q: In a tree, older, nonfunctioning xylem [ZYE-lum] is called what?
e: Heartwood sits happily retired at the tree's very center, staying strong and sturdy long after it stops carrying sap.

q: Different cell junctions are used to connect neighboring cells as needed for their functions. Which of the following options describes a situation that is utilizing desmosomes [DEZ-muh-sohms]?
a: In developing embryos, ions can travel through a pore connecting the two membranes of adjacent cells to permit rapid cell communication
Muscle cells are joined to form a sturdy sheet
Skin cells are joined to make a barrier impervious to even water
In a plant cell, small solutes in the cytoplasm will travel from cell to cell
e: Desmosomes act like super-strong buttons, riveting pulling muscle cells into one tough sheet so they never tear apart!

q: If a solution of phospholipids were dropped into a non-polar liquid, which of the following would MOST likely happen:
a: the fatty acid tails would be stripped from the phosphate heads
the phospholipids would mix evenly in the non-polar liquid
micelles (read as: MY-CELLS) would form with polar heads on the outside
micelles would form with polar heads on the inside
e: Water-loving heads huddle shyly together on the inside to hide from oily liquid, forming a neat little ball!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding short day plants?
a: Flowering occurs when night length is less than critical length
Continuity of darkness is crucial; flowering will not occur if darkness is interrupted by a momentary light flash
Short day plants are synonymous with long night plants
Photoperiod can be detected via phytochromes
e: Short-day plants are truly night lovers, so they bloom only when dark nights are extra long, not short!

q: John Gurdon studied totipotency [toh-TIH-pah-ten-see] by implanting a nucleus from a fully-differentiated frog cell into enucleated egg cells. Which of the following best describes what he observed about the egg?
a: It continued to divide, but stopped development prior to forming a tadpole
It continued to divide and developed into a tadpole as normal
It did not begin to divide after nucleation
It continued to divide, but skipped the tadpole stage and formed a frog
e: The egg began dividing with its transplanted nucleus, but stopped growing before it could ever become a tadpole.

q: Which of the following hormones promotes bud formation?
e: Cytokinins act like cheerful messengers, encouraging resting plant stems to wake up and sprout brand-new buds!

q: In the lac [lack] operon, allolactose can be classified as what?
e: Allolactose acts as an inducer, nudging the stubborn blocker away so the cell's machinery can happily read the gene!

q: Which of the following functions is least important in the open circulatory system of insects?
e: Bugs breathe through tiny body tubes, so their sloshing blood leaves oxygen delivery to them!

q: While on holiday in Mexico, you note a local vendor selling arrow plant seed pods that jump due the presence of an immature insect that is violently throwing itself from side to side in the seed pod. The insect responsible for this would be a member of what insect order?
e: Inside that jumping bean is a tiny baby moth from the Lepidoptera family, happily doing gymnastics to stay cool!

q: What scientific family does the Aardwolf belong to?
e: Even though it munches on termites, this shy striped critter belongs to Hyaenidae, the hyena family.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the human body:
a: there are substantial numbers of lymph nodes in the wall of the large intestine
veins have comparatively thick walls with more muscle than arteries
there are two layers of smooth muscle in the walls of the small intestine
the small intestine is longer than the large intestine
e: Arteries are the true muscular heavyweights here, while gentle veins have thinner, stretchier walls to guide blood home.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about plant physiology?
a: Meristematic [meh-rih-stuh-MAT-ic} tissue located at the tips of stems and roots forms the apical [A-pik-ul] meristems [MEH-rih-stems]
Some plants, like shrubs, have lateral meristems
Vascular and cork cambium [KAM-bee-um] are produced by apical meristems
Intercalary [In-TER-cah-lair-ee] meristems allow grass to grow even after it has been mowed
e: Apical tips help plants grow super tall, but wide woody stems get their cambium from lateral helpers instead!

q: What is the organ, found in birds and some invertebrates, that is used to temporarily store food, but also aids in preliminary digestion?
e: Think of the crop as a bird's built-in lunchbox, saving delicious seeds and softening them up for later.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of negative feedback?
a: High blood glucose causing insulin release
Secretion of cortisol inhibiting ACTH release
Release of platelet activating factor during clotting
e: Clotting platelets call in more and more helpful buddies, building a team instead of slowing down.

q: The cloaca (read as: klo-AY-ka) is a reproductive structure of:
e: A female bird uses her cloaca as a neat, all-in-one doorway for laying eggs and tidying up.

q: Which of the following lengths of DNA would be least likely to be unwound by a passive helicase?
e: G and C hold hands with three super-strong bonds, clinging together way too tightly to be unzipped easily!

q: The gram stain can be used to distinguish between different prokaryotes [proh-KAR-ee-ohts] based on which of the following?
e: The colorful Gram stain checks the thickness of a bacterium's tiny cell wall coat to tell who is who.

q: Which of the following parts of B and T cells bind to antigens?
e: The variable region can change its shape like magical clay to catch sneaky germ invaders!

q: Which of the following habitat and life history combinations would select for the production of a large brood size?
e: In the chilly Arctic summer, babies born ready to run let busy parents raise lots of little adventurers at once.

q: Which of the following organisms is haploid?
e: Male ants hatch from unfertilized eggs, so they pack only one single set of instructions inside!

q: The proboscis [proh-BOS-kis] is used primarily by invertebrates to perform which of the following functions?
e: A proboscis is like a built-in bendy straw that hungry bugs use to sip sweet flower juice.

q: Which of the following processes would be least similar in terms of ATP production between normal adipose tissue and brown adipose tissue?
e: Brown fat uses its electron transport chain like a warm little heater to make heat instead of storing energy!

q: Caspases are apoptosis-promoting enzymes that perform what function?
e: Caspases act like tiny scissors, neatly snipping protein bonds apart when a tired old cell needs to recycle itself.

q: Which of the following classes of macromolecules can be digested by salivary amylase?
e: Amylase in your spit starts chomping on starchy carbohydrates the second you take a bite of yummy bread!

q: How many legs is it biologically impossible for a centipede to have?
e: Centipedes always have an odd number of leg pairs, which means having fifty pairs—or one hundred legs—is completely impossible.

q: Limited food, decreased water, and loss of available nesting sites are likely to have which of the following impacts on a population?
e: When snacks and cozy homes run out, the neighborhood simply cannot hold as many happy neighbors anymore.

q: To which biological phylum do all mammals, birds and reptiles belong?
e: Mammals, birds, and reptiles all belong to Chordata because they share the grand adventure of having a backbone!

q: Loss of the retinoblastoma gene product, Rb, causes cancer by affecting which of the following portions of the cell cycle?
e: Think of Rb as a sleepy crossing guard at the G1/S checkpoint; when it goes missing, cells rush wildly ahead into dividing!

q: Which of the following statements does NOT correctly describe the adaptive immune system?
a: T cells finish maturation in the bone marrow
B cells generate antibodies through VDJ recombination
T cells recognize and destroy infected cells
Maternal antibodies can cross the placenta
e: Brave little T cells start out in bone marrow, but they actually travel to the thymus school to finish growing up.

q: G-protein coupled receptors regulate various cell signaling events in a cell. How many transmembrane segments are typically found in these receptors?
e: This tiny receptor weaves back and forth through the cell's outer wall exactly seven times, like thread stitching a cozy seam.

q: In beats per minute, what is the normal range of resting heart rates in adults?
e: When an adult sits quietly, their faithful heart taps out a calm rhythm of sixty to one hundred beats each minute.

q: Which of the following is closest to the diameter of a plasmodesmata (read as: PLAS-mo-dez-MAH-tah):
e: These secret plant tunnels are wonderfully tiny, measuring just sixty nanometers across so neighboring cells can whisper to each other.

q: What is the function of the operculum [oh-PURR-kyoo-lum] in fish?
e: Like a shiny little shield, this bony flap keeps a fish's delicate gills safe and sound from harm.

q: Which of the following processes results in a net reduction in the amount of atmospheric carbon dioxide?
e: Hungry green leaves gulp down carbon dioxide from the air during photosynthesis to make sweet snacks for themselves!

q: In which of the following habitats would you expect to find the highest productivity AND lowest diversity of species?
e: Salt marshes are super tough places where few species can survive, but the hardy grasses that do thrive grow wildly fast.

q: As read from 5 prime to 3 prime, which of the following codons could a release factor bind to?
e: The codon UAA acts just like a bright red stop sign, inviting a release factor to finish the protein.

q: Some disease-causing microbes attack the body by turning on or off specific signal transduction pathways. In the disease cholera, for example, a toxin from the bacterium Vibrio cholera enters intestinal cells and chemically modifies G proteins. Once modified, the G proteins can no longer cleave GTP into GDP. Which of the following would you expect to see within the intestinal cells of a person with cholera?
a: The G proteins remain activated and continually activate adenylyl cylase
The G proteins cannot become activated and cannot activate adenylyl cylase
The G protein subunits do not separate from each other
The receptor in the membrane is continually activated
e: The toxin jams the G protein's switch on, so it never stops shouting at adenylyl cyclase to keep running!

q: Which of the following properties of double-stranded DNA makes DNA ligase necessary for successful replication?
a: Only complementary bases bond to each other
A complementary RNA primer can bind to DNA
It can only be synthesized in the 5-prime-to-3-prime direction
The double helix must be untwisted for replication
e: Cell builders can only construct DNA in one direction, leaving little backward puzzle pieces that ligase must glue together.

q: Steroids can be classified as which of the following types of biomacromolecule?
e: Even though steroids act like busy messengers, their oily, water-hating nature means they belong to the lipid family.

q: Duchenne [duh-SHEEN] muscular dystrophy is the result of a recessive disease allele [uh-LEEL] for a gene on the X-chromosome. Which of the following is true regarding inheritance of the disease?
a: Females have twice the chance of developing it, because they have two X chromosomes
Mothers with the disease allele can pass it with equal probability to sons or daughters
Inbreeding has no effect on the likelihood of inheriting this disease
An affected son is always produced if his father has the disease allele
e: A mother flips a coin with her X chromosomes, so sons and daughters have the exact same chance of inheriting it.

q: The American bullfrog is a prolific hunter and can eat a wide variety of foods, including native western pond turtles and mice. Currently, western pond turtles are listed as an endangered species. Which of the following best explains why turtle populations would be more impacted than mice by the introduction of bullfrogs?
a: Bullfrogs like to eat turtles more than they like to eat mice
Turtles run slower than mice so they can't get away from the bullfrogs
Turtles have a much longer generation time than mice
e: While mice have babies quickly, patient turtles take many years to grow up, making it much harder for their population to bounce back.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between peptoids, or poly-N-substituted glycines, and proteins?
a: Peptoids have less constrained secondary structure than proteins
Peptoids cannot possess tertiary structure, while proteins can
Peptoids form more stable alpha helices than proteins
Peptoids form more stable beta sheets than proteins
e: Peptoids have side chains attached to nitrogen instead of carbon, giving them much floppier, less rigid shapes than neat proteins.

q: The LH surge just prior to ovulation in mammals is thought to be triggered by a surge in what other hormone?
e: A big rush of estradiol sends a cheering signal that sparks the sudden leap in LH just before ovulation!

q: Which of the following organisms is an example of a bivalve?
e: An oyster is a classic bivalve because it lives snugly inside two hinged shells that snap together like a book.

q: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Miller-Urey [MILL-er YOO-ree] experiment test conditions for the chemical origins of life?
e: In their famous soup recipe for ancient Earth, the scientists cooked with methane and ammonia, completely leaving out carbon dioxide.

q: In regard to human anatomy, with which of the following is Wolff's law concerned?
a: The shape of bone being determined by mechanical and gravitational stresses
The negative feedback loops that control production of thyroid hormone
The forces generated by isotonic contractions of skeletal muscle
The electrical potential of resting cardiac cells
e: Wolff noticed that living bones reshape and grow stronger right where daily gravity and heavy stomps press on them.

q: Which period involved a major extinction event that included the dinosaurs?
a: Between the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras
Between the Phanerozoic and the Precambrian eras
Between the Mesozoic and Cenozoic eras
Between the Precambrian and Paleozoic eras
e: The giant asteroid closed the curtain on the dinosaur-filled Mesozoic era, waving hello to the new Cenozoic world of mammals.

q: Eggs exit a chicken's body through what specific structure:
e: A chicken's cloaca is like a magical, all-in-one backdoor that gently guides an egg out into the world.

q: Baker's yeast is an example of what type of fungi?
e: Baker's yeast belongs to the ascomycete family because these bubbly little fungi tuck their spores inside tiny, cozy microscopic sacs.

q: Eukaryotic [yoo-KAR-ee-oh-tik] genes are composed of introns and exons. Which of the following eukaryotes [yoo-KAR-ee-ohts] would have the shortest intron size?
e: Tiny, busy yeast cells like to travel light, keeping their extra gene pieces, called introns, delightfully short and tidy.

q: In the lipid membranes of cells, there are multipass proteins that are partly within the lipid bilayer and partly outside of the lipid bilayer. Through which of the following forces do these proteins achieve this position relative to the membrane?
e: These proteins weave in and out because their water-loving parts reach outside, while their oily parts snuggle safely inside the membrane.

q: Which of the following is NOT a cellular structure that functions to increase surface area and maximize the performance of cellular processes?
e: While other cell parts fold to make room, tiny hair-like pili act like little sticky fingers to help bacteria cling to things.

q: Plasmids are autonomously replicating circles of DNA containing one or a few genes. How many plasmids may a single bacterium carry?
e: Bacteria love collecting tiny DNA rings, and there is no fixed limit to how many can join the party!

q: What is the name of the copper-rich protein that creates the blue blood in the Antarctic octopus?
e: Hemocyanin uses shiny bits of copper to ferry oxygen through freezing seas, turning the octopus's blood a magical royal blue.

q: What chemicals do peroxisomes [pe-ro-KSI-sohms] use to oxidize other compounds?
e: Peroxisomes use bubbly hydrogen peroxide like a zippy clean-up potion, safely dissolving trash inside the busy cell.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a human disease caused by a recessive allele that fails to produce a viable cellular protein?
e: Turner's syndrome happens when an entire X chromosome goes missing, rather than a single broken gene quietly snoozing.

q: Pseudogenes are commonly found in the genome of an organism. Which of the following describes the most likely mechanism of how these features arose?
e: When DNA accidentally photocopies a gene through duplication, the spare copy can break down and become a quiet, resting pseudogene.

q: What is the most appropriate term for the genetic character of an organism having a pair of identical alleles for a certain trait:
e: Being homozygous means having two identical gene twins happily teaming up to build the exact same trait.

q: The basal lamina is a long thin structure that is essential for the stability of body cells. Which of the following cell classes is NOT typically underlain or surrounded by the basal lamina?
e: Tough cartilage cells float inside their own rubbery cushions, so they do not need a basal lamina carpet beneath them.

q: Which of the following is thought to have been the beneficial effect of two entire genome duplication events in the vertebrate lineage?
a: More copies of each gene per cell were insurance against DNA damage from increased solar radiation
Polyploid animals were more likely to have one good copy of each gene
One copy of a duplicated gene was free to take on new functions
Four copies of each gene meant stronger gene responses
e: When ancient animals got an extra copy of their genes, the spare was free to dream up brand-new superpowers!

q: If the human SRY gene is inactivated in the first week of gestation, which of the following will occur:
a: the embryo will continue as a male
the embryo will remain in a quiescent state
e: Without the SRY switch clicking on to start male development, the embryo naturally follows the path to remain female.

q: What causes the sound of a heartbeat?
e: That steady lub-dub music is actually the sound of your heart's tiny doorway valves gently snapping shut behind rushing blood.

q: Plant cells are distinguished from animal cells by having:
a: A large central vacuole, chloroplasts, and a cell wall made of cellulose
A large central vacuole, mitochondria, and a nucleus
A cell wall made of cellulose, Golgi apparatus, and chloroplasts
e: Plants stay proud and green using tough cellulose walls, sun-catching chloroplasts, and giant water vacuoles that animals simply lack.

q: In which of the following glands do hematopoietic [hi-mat-oh- poi-EE-tik] stem cells develop into T cells?
e: The thymus acts like a superhero academy, training young stem cells until they graduate into brave, disease-fighting T cells!

q: Which of the following amino acids would be most likely found in the intramembrane domain of a surface receptor protein?
e: Water-fearing phenylalanine loves hiding inside the oily middle of the membrane, where it can stay cozy and dry.

q: What do amoebas use in order to move around?
e: Amoebas squish their bodies forward by reaching out goofy, temporary blob-arms called pseudopodia to pull themselves along.

q: Which of the following BEST describes what the term virulence means:
a: the specificity of a virus to cause disease in a certain host
the ability of a microbe to cause cellular damage
any transmissible disease caused by a microbe
the degree to which a microbe causes disease or harm to its host
e: Virulence tells us how naughty a germ is by measuring just how much harm it can cause its host.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of photorespiration:
a: the process whereby primitive bacteria use light to help oxidize inorganic molecules
the competition of carbon dioxide and molecular oxygen for Rubisco
the gaining of chemical energy in photosynthesis
the loss of reduced electrons from photosystem one
e: Plant helper Rubisco wants carbon dioxide, but nosy oxygen barges in to steal its attention, starting a messy tug-of-war!

q: Cyclic photophosphorylation (read as: FE-te-fohs-fohr-i-LAY- shon) functions mainly for which of the following purposes?
a: Recycling electrons resulting from the absorption of light in Photosystem I
e: Sunlight sends tiny electrons on a fun loop-de-loop ride, recycling them right back to where they started.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of an r-selected species?
a: The mother produces a large number of eggs that suffer heavy predation
The mother reaches sexual maturity early in life
The parents provide long-term care for the offspring
The species is more successful in unstable environments
e: These speedy critters have hundreds of babies at once, wave goodbye, and let them grow up without any babysitting!

q: In a typical mouse mammalian research model, which type of epithelial [eh-pih-THEEL-ee-ul] cell would be most prevalent lining kidney tubules?
e: Inside the mouse's busy kidneys, neat little cube-shaped cells stand side by side, tidying up the fluid like tiny building blocks.

q: Which of the following best describes adaptive immunity?
a: It includes external barriers such as secretions from mucous membranes
It is found in both vertebrates and invertebrates
It includes an interaction of pathogens, antibodies, and lymphocytes [LIM-fuh-syts]
e: Clever defender cells train custom-made tags called antibodies to chase down and tackle specific sneaky germs!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of energy coupling?
a: An ion releases energy as it travels through an ion channel down its concentration gradient
A kinase hydrolyzes ATP for energy to catalyze a reaction
A transport molecule uses energy from one molecule going down its concentration gradient to power transport of another molecule up its gradient
As protons move down their concentration gradient, ATP synthase gathers energy to catalyze the synthesis of ATP
e: Sliding downhill is fun, but if an ion rides alone without powering another job, it is not a team-up.

q: To diagnose whooping cough, which of the following culture media is the medium of choice for bacterial incubation?
a: Xylose lysine deoxycholate agar (read as: ZY-les LY-seen dee-ohk-see-KE-layt)
e: Picky whooping cough germs love growing on charcoal-rich Regan-Lowe jelly, their favorite cozy dinner plate!

q: What is the most immediate role for the protons produced from water photolysis [foh-TOL-uh-sis] during photosynthesis?
a: React with oxygen to make water
Acidify the mitochondrial matrix and provide fuel for chemiosmosis
Contribute to the proton gradient in the thylakoid and ultimately provide energy to make ATP
Combine with carbon dioxide during sugar synthesis
e: Split water drops pack tiny protons together like water behind a dam, building power to spin out fresh energy!

q: Which of the following processes is NOT correctly matched with the role it plays in the global nitrogen cycle?
a: Nitrogen fixation with the Haber-Bosch process
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria with ammonia produced from nitrogen gas
Legume root nodules with nitrate produced from ammonia
Denitrification [dee-ny-truh-fi-KAY-shuhn] with nitrogen gas produced from nitrates
e: Helpful root bugs turn air into ammonia for plants, leaving the job of making nitrates to other soil critters.

q: In Barbara McClintock's famous experiments revealing the existence of transposable genes, she primarily used which of the following as her experimental organism:
e: By watching rainbow kernels on ears of corn, a brilliant scientist saw lively genes jumping all over the place!

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding water balance in the mammalian body?
a: Dehydration increases the osmolality of blood
Vasopressin is produced by the adrenal gland
Renin inhibits the conversion of angiotensinogen [an-jee-oh-ten- SIN-oh-jen] to angiotensin [an-jee-oh-TEN-sin] two
Aldosterone [al-DOSS-ter-own] inhibits sodium absorption in the distal tubules
e: When you are thirsty and lose water, your blood gets extra crowded with salts, just like thick syrup.

q: All of the following human genetic haplogroup names are shared between Y-chromosome and mitochondrial DNA haplogroups EXCEPT:
e: Haplogroup U is special because it only travels down the mother's side in mitochondrial DNA, never through the Y-chromosome.

q: Which of the following is the target tissue of the hormone leptin where it binds with LepRB (read as: L, E, P, R, B) receptors:
e: Leptin sends a cheerful postcard straight to your brain's hypothalamus, whispering that your tummy is completely full.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of chloroplasts:
