a: they are relatively large organelles and can exceed 3 microns long
thay have smaller ribosomes than are found in the plant cytosol
they contain thylakoid (read as: THY-la-koid) stacks
their numbers are controlled primarily by the cell's nuclear genes that control division
e: Chloroplasts act like independent little roommates, dividing on their own schedule rather than waiting for the nucleus to tell them.

q: All of the following changes would result in an increase in blood pressure, except:
e: Widening the body's tiny blood pipes gives blood more room to stroll, which gently lowers the pressure!

q: All of the following pairs of structures are homologous [huh- MOL-uh-guhs], EXCEPT:
a: The wing of a bat and the wing of a bird
The leg of a human and the leg of a centipede
The scales on a bird's legs and the scales on a lizard
The shell of a clam and the shell of a snail
e: Though both are built for walking, human and centipede legs grew from completely different ancient family blueprints.

q: Which of the following describes the location of the 3-prime UTR in a strand of eukaryotic mRNA?
a: Between the transcription start site and the start codon
Between the stop codon and the poly-A tail
e: This cozy untranslated stretch rests quietly between the gene's stop sign and its long tail of A's.

q: Of the seven species of sea turtles, six are found in U.S. waters. Which of the following species of sea turtles is NOT found in U.S. waters?
e: The sleepy flatback turtle is a homebody who prefers splashing near Australia and never visits American shores.

q: Which of the following vitamins is NOT synthesized by plants or animals?
e: Plants and animals cannot bake vitamin B12; only clever little bacteria know the secret recipe!

q: Which of the following human cell types do NOT perform aerobic respiration?
e: Red blood cells carry oxygen to everyone else, but generously deliver it without breathing any of it themselves!

q: What location in a seed is equivalent to the embryonic leaf?
e: Tucked snug inside every sleepy seed, cotyledons are tiny baby leaves ready to unfurl and feed the growing plant.

q: Which of the following is true regarding the differences between New World and Old World monkeys?
a: New World monkeys evolved from prosimians, while Old World monkeys evolved from anthropoids
New World monkeys are all arboreal, while Old World monkeys include some ground- dwelling species
New World monkeys lack prehensile tails, while Old World monkeys have prehensile tails
New World monkeys have downward pointed noses, while Old World monkeys have flat, spreading noses
e: Every New World monkey loves living high in the trees, but some Old World cousins prefer hanging out on the ground.

q: What is the scientific name for the Bald Eagle?
e: The bald eagle is known as Haliaeetus leucocephalus, which neatly translates to white-headed sea eagle.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding glycogen:
a: glycogen synthesis is endergonic (read as: en-der-GONE-ick)
glycogen side branches have beta 1,4 linkages
glycogen in the human liver often has more than 10,000 glucose monomers
e: Glycogen builds its bushy energy branches using alpha connections, never beta ones, which makes that statement false.

q: In photosynthesis, where do electrons derived from water first enter the process?
e: When water gets split, its eager electrons leap straight into photosystem two to kick off their grand solar adventure.

q: Which of the following fish is endemic to the island of Cozumel?
e: Showing off bright neon stripes, the shy splendid toadfish makes its cozy home only around the island of Cozumel.

q: Which of the following marine snails produces a deadly toxin?
e: Do not let its pretty shell fool you! The geographic cone snail hides a tiny venomous harpoon that can be deadly.

q: Which of the following examples is NOT evidence for evolution from a common ancestor?
a: All living things have basic cell processes that are similar and use similar molecules
Hox genes, or homeotic genes, control vertebrate body plans and are homologous in all vertebrates
Even though snakes don't have legs, some snake embryos have limb buds during development similar to other reptile embryos
Bats and birds both have wings that are adaptations for flying
e: Bats and birds both fly, but they invented their wings separately instead of inheriting them from a shared flying ancestor.
